disease_assertions.locator: dismissal_ledger_current.md DIS-37 PREMISE: PubMed counts of 2026-10-19; R3 note section 1.3
disease_assertions.note: The repository records WWOX-with-mTOR-or-AMPK counts at title and abstract level and a blocked WWOX/mTOR paper whose full text is unread; direction in a WWOX-deficient neural system is not established here; protein-level readouts exist in non-neural carcinoma cells (PMID 24008736).
disease_assertions.source: DIS-37 premise and R3 note 1.3

a_woree_evaluation_would_have_to_measure: a repeated, instrument-matched baseline before any exposure, in a form that can move in a profoundly impaired child (growth-scale or raw-score forms rather than standard scores); no measurement of the scatter of an untreated interval in WOREE is established here (the repository's series have one timepoint per patient; no wider search was run)
a pharmacodynamic anchor: none exists for any WWOX-directed intervention (CLAIM 046), so engagement of the intended target cannot be shown at all
one prespecified endpoint with a rescue or withdrawal rule written before the observation window opens
survival, reported beside whatever endpoint is chosen
seizures only as a separate, declared family: a countable fraction, a diary or agreed reconstruction rule, and the seizure-free stratum reported apart (it is prognostic, not a treatment effect)
and_could_not_claim: disease modification or developmental benefit: the developmental-delay row of the one WOREE series reporting a response is identical in every column and two of the three responders had died
that seizure control protects development (CLAIM 031 forbids counting any symptomatic outcome as disease modification)
benefit from a pharmacodynamic move, a global impression or an own-baseline comparison
any effect smaller than the instrument's own untreated scatter

the word protection: in the human precedents read for this frame none measured the preservation of a function that would otherwise have been lost; the repository's mouse rescue studies are outside this frame and the scope of 'this corpus' is not defined, so no wider negative is established here

mission_dimensions.route_note: qualified by one curated card: EB-MTOR-AX-01; Track is read only from the card(s) that state it - EB-MTOR-AX-01 state(s) a route and no Track (written before Track was qualified)

must_never: No score, rank, probability or blended index. 'Non-dominated' would be a statement about visible dimensions, never a number.
No dose, route, schedule, course or paediatric suitability. Accessibility of a drug, diet or supplement does not prove paediatric suitability.
A computational prediction is not DATO. No engine was run for this card.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE and is never promoted to WWOX evidence.
A missing hit is not proof of absence.
Symptomatic benefit is not slowing of disease; the word 'protection' is not licensed by any evidence on this card.
Where CLAIM 011 has been narrowed, 'dose-dependent' does not stand.
Nothing here is medical advice; it supports discussion with a treating clinical team and never substitutes for one.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: UNKNOWN: no WOREE-relevant endpoint is supported for this class
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: none in a WWOX-deficient neural system (non-neural carcinoma cells have protein-level readouts, PMID 24008736); the class evidence comes from genetic mTOR-pathway reduction in a Tsc1 model (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: the infant record is in tuberous sclerosis, an mTOR-driven disease; it does not transfer to WOREE

p4_roadmap_fields.evidence_pro_contra: Visible: infant adverse-effect record and the monitoring items the authors name. Absent: any benefit signal in WOREE.
p4_roadmap_fields.identity: Sirolimus, mTOR-inhibitor class; no formulation, dose, trough target or schedule is carried.
p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Origin: tuberous sclerosis infants (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE). Bridge to WOREE: not established.
p4_roadmap_fields.next_measure: Does the blocked WWOX/mTOR paper (full text unread) report a direction of mTOR activity in a WWOX-deficient neural system?
p4_roadmap_fields.novelty_for_woree: Not found in the research for a WWOX-deficient neural system at this card's depth. The mTOR/autophagy stubs and the blocked paper are an owed read (FT-074; DIS-37 revival trigger).
p4_roadmap_fields.paediatrics_and_interactions: A paediatric record exists for this class in another disease; it is not an authorisation for this one and not a suitability statement. Interactions: UNKNOWN.
p4_roadmap_fields.path_and_objective: Declared BENEFICIO_PRECOCE for this card because only the safety record is visible; the pathway rationale belongs to the deep-recovery path (scientist-a's cards), which this card does not enter.
p4_roadmap_fields.sources: R3 note 1.5 (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE): in 21 infants with tuberous sclerosis «All 21 had at least one adverse effect», mainly haematological and metabolic, no grade 4 or 5 and no discontinuation for an adverse effect; in ten neonatal-unit infants all had raised triglycerides; an infant spontaneous-report reporting ratio the authors call hypothesis-generating. The statement that sirolimus hyperlipidaemia is dose-dependent is a literature claim not shown in the infant cohort (R3 note section 5); no dose-response claim is carried here.
p4_roadmap_fields.status: ASTENSIONE. Missing datum: a direction of mTOR activity in a WWOX-deficient neural system and any WOREE endpoint.
p4_roadmap_fields.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Clinical census 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven unfiltered queries on ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the one WOREE record is an observational registry and natural-history study. Its own caution binds this card: «A missing hit does not prove that no study exists.» An NCT number proves neither recruitment nor first dosing.
p4_roadmap_fields.value_added: Shows that an infant safety record can exist while the benefit axis is empty, so safety visibility is not candidacy.
p4_roadmap_fields.verification_scope: R3 readings: blind locator audit OWED (declared in that note). This card: audit OWED.

evidence_against: SPECIFICITY FAILED: lithium suppressed the provoked seizure in all three genotypes, wild type included (Figure 7d; entries 0, 22).

The causal attribution to GSK3beta rests on lithium alone; the paper's own Discussion names lithium's other documented actions, including Wnt/beta-catenin-dependent effects (entry 3). Lithium acts on many targets besides GSK3beta.

The only cell-line source (Wang 2012, PMID 22193544) reports Ser9 phosphorylation unchanged during retinoic-acid differentiation of SH-SY5Y cells, while WWOX rose (entry 5): that is a WWOX-gain, differentiation context, not a WWOX-loss measurement, and must not be read as a knockdown result; the knockdown experiment of that paper measured Tau phosphorylation (entry 8), not Ser9.
Direction conflict (INFERENZA): beta-catenin stabilisation by lithium would push an axis that is already raised in WWOX-loss organoids (map record R-04, axis M5; card P4-D-02).
Different control groups and schedules for lithium and ethosuximide inside one figure (entries 27, 28): the two drugs are not compared on equal terms.
A clinical anticonvulsant effect would be symptomatic: CLAIM 031 states that seizure control does not buy development.

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Symptomatic seizure suppression in a provoked-seizure assay; not WWOX-specific (wild type responds). Not deep recovery; WWOX function would remain lost. Track B: no allele-specific datum.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was opened for this card. Every locator is an existing entry of the deep-dive manifests PMID32000863.json and PMID22193544.json; the figure statements are those entries' own.
not_known: Whether lithium does anything in a Wwox-deficient system that it does not do in a wild-type one (the one experiment that tested it answered no).
Whether lithium moves GSK3beta Ser9 phosphorylation or kinase activity in a Wwox-null brain: lithium's effect on the Ser9 readout was not measured in this system.

Whether GSK3beta abundance or Ser9 state tracks activity here: the sources are in tension and no kinase-activity assay exists in WWOX-deficient cells or tissue (the kinase assays of the cell-line paper are cell-free, with purified recombinant proteins, and show WWOX protein lowering GSK3beta-driven Tau phosphorylation in vitro). The cell-line paper reports phospho-Ser9 unchanged along a retinoic-acid time course while WWOX rises; no experiment in it manipulates WWOX and reads Ser9, and the phrase 'S9-independent' occurs nowhere in its text; the only tissue datum (Wwox-null brain, cerebellum, hippocampus and cortex; the legend says postnatal day 20 and the Methods say 14) reports LOWER phospho-Ser9, as a ratio to beta-actin, with representative results of four independent experiments and the number of animals not stated (registry CLAIM 035 Evidence boundary, BATCH_20261120_001; the earlier wording of this item, 'S9-independent inhibition', is withdrawn) [IT59 2026-11-20 packet change].
Whether the null-genotype hypersusceptibility is a driver of the developmental phenotype or an amplifier on a malformed brain (entry 6).
Whether the wild-type response is floor-limited in a way that hides a genotype difference.
Any allele-specific datum (Q230P class or splice allele): none exists for lithium.
Net direction on the Wnt axis: lithium stabilises beta-catenin, and WWOX-loss organoids show nuclear beta-catenin already raised (card P4-D-02).

evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Engineered null mouse versus a missense or compound human context; a provoked-seizure score in preweaning pups versus a human epilepsy; one laboratory.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN beyond non-specific seizure suppression; direction on the Wnt axis possibly adverse (INFERENZA).
p4_card.identity: Lithium (the salt used in the mouse experiment: lithium chloride; the clinical compound class is lithium carbonate), used in the one WWOX experiment as a tool inhibitor of GSK3beta. Map records R-04 (repurposing) and N-02 (negative translation) describe the same candidate and are linked to this one card.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Symptomatic seizure suppression is the only endpoint ever tested in a WWOX system; it is non-specific (wild type responds equally). A WWOX-specific disease-modifying rationale is not supported by the primary data. Transfer to the reference genotype: not established.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: GSK3beta (among many); claimed: inhibits a kinase de-repressed by WWOX loss; the de-repression is read from a single Ser9 phosphorylation blot; the attribution of the seizure effect to GSK3beta rests on lithium alone.
p4_card.next_measurement: A provoked-seizure arm with an explicit, tested null versus wild-type contrast and the interaction reported, or a different GSK3beta inhibitor under the same design; and a kinase-activity or substrate-phosphorylation readout in a Wwox-null system. Until then no genotype-specific claim is available. The substrate-phosphorylation readout is now DESIGNED, not measured: tau phospho-sites over total tau, Ser9 over TOTAL GSK3beta (not over actin) and beta-catenin, in the cortex of the neuronal-deletion line at postnatal day 17, with a decision per outcome fixed before data (SCI design v2.2 and v3.1, hypothesis level, no data) [IT59 2026-11-20 packet change].
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Already studied once (Cheng 2020, one laboratory, one experiment). Not new; the question is whether the result means what it was read as meaning.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use. The label states paediatric safety and effectiveness as established for monotherapy of bipolar I disorder at ages 7 to 17 and not established below 7; that is a statement for another indication and is not a paediatric suitability for WWOX-DEE [IT59 2026-11-20 packet change].
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A (allele-blind); not deep recovery.
p4_card.pharmacology: Approved compound (class level, from map record R-04) with a narrow therapeutic index and monitoring needs; CNS exposure is not in doubt. Nothing here is a statement about exposure in WWOX-DEE. Label facts, read at source by a blind verifier on 2026-11-20 (US label record, class level, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE): a boxed warning that lithium toxicity is closely related to serum concentration and can occur at doses close to therapeutic concentrations; neurological signs of toxicity include ataxia and, among severe manifestations, seizure, and in rare cases neurological sequelae may persist after discontinuation and may be associated with cerebellar atrophy (the label hedges); lithium is concentrated in the thyroid and can lead to hypothyroidism (hyperthyroidism cases are also reported); in pregnancy the label says lithium may cause harm and names a floppy baby syndrome in neonates exposed late in pregnancy [IT59 2026-11-20 packet change].

disease_assertions.endpoint: log2 shift, knockout minus wild type
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: PDK1 -0.34 (mean of log2(CPM+1), knockout minus wild type; log2 of the ratio of mean CPM is -0.36) and -0.39 (log2 of the ratio of mean median-of-ratios counts, which is the IT5 same-sets re-analysis), the same six libraries; PDK1 is in neither deposited list and is lower in sign only (lower in all four knockout libraries than in both wild-type libraries, a pattern that is common in this deposit: of 2,804 genes with mean CPM within 1.5-fold of PDK1's, 663, 24 percent, are lower in all four knockout libraries than in both wild-type libraries and 570, 20 percent, higher, against about 6.7 percent each way expected for exchangeable 4 against 2 libraries; inside the single-gene null, p about 0.30, where the null is not defined in the held files, an empirical version gives 0.27 to 0.39, and a recompute of the share of expression-matched genes with an equal or larger shift gave 0.33 to 0.35; with 4 against 2 libraries no rank test can reach a two-sided P below 0.13, and a Welch t-test on log2(CPM+1) would give about 0.03 and is not meaningful with 2 wild-type libraries; the datum is the absence of support for a raised PDK1, not a demonstrated decrease; see card I01); the PDK/PDH set +0.17 (P 0.22 from the repository's own set test, rerun at 0.2265; the set is not defined in the held files and the +0.17 is not reproduced: plausible memberships tried gave +0.15 to +0.24, and a second reader's random sets of plausible membership gave P 0.33 to 0.81; the set mean averages away PDHA1, PDPR and LDHA, which are in the authors' up list at adjusted P 5.8E-10, 1.3E-04 and 4.9E-06, and PDK3, higher in all four knockout libraries at 1.55 times, nominal P 7.39E-03, adjusted P 5.65E-02); the LDH-to-PDH transcript ratio depends on the pairing (log2 of (LDHA+LDHB) over (PDHA1+PDHB+DLAT+DLD), knockout minus wild type, -0.14; LDHA over PDHA1 0.72 against 0.86, three of four knockout libraries below both wild-type libraries; LDHA over (PDHA1+PDHB) 0.54 against 0.56), and no pairing was fixed in advance in the held sources. EXPLORATORY NEGATIVES: transcripts are not PDH activity, flux or metabolite, and do not show that PDH or lactate are normal. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-283, SCI's blind-checked wording] In two mouse tissues of one study (GSE158681 hippocampus, GSE158682 cortex; P17; gene TPM = sum of the gene's transcripts; n is the library, assumed one animal each) Pdk3 does not meet the anchor-size rule (ratio of arm means 1.2 or more with every deficient library above every control library) in either primary comparison: global null KO against wild type hippocampus 0.689 (n 2 v 3, all knockout below), neuron-targeted KO against control cortex 1.020 (n 3 v 4, overlapping). Secondary arms: Synapsin-Cre hippocampus 1.089 (n 3 v 2, overlapping), nestin-Cre hippocampus 0.913 (n 2 v 2). The 1.55 times of GSE156243 (a CPM ratio, 4 v 2 libraries; raw counts 1.75) is therefore not replicated in these mouse tissues and rests on one deposit. Every deficient arm has fewer oligodendrocyte transcripts (Plp1 0.17 to 0.49 of control) and more Gfap (1.6 to 4.3 times), so each ratio is a whole-tissue mixture ratio. Pdk1 meets the lower rule (ratio 0.83 or less with every deficient library below every control) only in the Synapsin-Cre hippocampus arm (0.661; n 3 v 2), where Pdk3 is 1.089 with overlapping libraries (25.24 below the control 25.70); the pattern is therefore absent only under the stated rule. In the cortex Pdk1 is 0.805, which meets the ratio limit but not the ordering (knockout 8.91 and 6.40 above control 4.30 and 5.74); global null 0.943; nestin-Cre 1.047. In GSE126075 (one shRNA-silenced and one untreated sample per cell type, merged CAGE TPM by gene symbol) the neuron pair's column totals differ about threefold (89,581 against 264,496), every gene in the silenced neuron sample is lower by a median 0.36, and WWOX CAGE signal is 1.15 times control in hNSC and 0.20 in neurons. The neuron PDK ratios (PDK3 0.33, PDK1 0.48) sit at that library-wide shift; for hNSC PDK1 is 0.69 and PDK3 0.91 (n of 1, no WWOX depletion in the signal). Descriptive only; not counted toward support or failure. The mouse arms are not a like-for-like test of the human organoid.

disease_assertions.endpoint: log2 shift, knockdown minus control, CAGE promoter sums (sign only)
disease_assertions.note: Recomputed from the deposit (one library per arm; PDK1 tags 263 against 51 in progenitors and 108 against 64 in day-14 neurons), the log2 ratio of the deposited TPM is -0.54 in progenitors and -1.07 in neurons. The neuron pair's gene-table column sums differ about threefold (summed TPM 89,581 against 264,496); normalising to those sums gives +0.49, while median re-centring over expressed genes gives -0.60 to -0.77 in progenitors and +0.34 to +0.50 in neurons depending on the gene filter (-0.74 and +0.41 with every gene detected in both libraries). The earlier centred values (-0.67 and +0.44) are matched to within 0.001 by median centring over genes with a pair-mean TPM of at least 10, a filter found after the fact, so they are filter-dependent rather than irreproducible; their original normalisation is not stated and their p of about 0.49 could not be reproduced. A Poisson half-width of about 0.45 around -0.67 excludes zero, and with one library per arm no decrease is demonstrated; the note is descriptive only. WWOX knockdown is shown by one Western blot in progenitors only (Supplementary Figure 1); the WWOX CAGE signal is 1.15 times control in progenitors and 0.20 in neurons (0.60 after normalising to the column sums). In the progenitor library PAX6, SOX2, HES5, FABP7 and SOX21 are lower while NES, VIM, HES1 and SLC1A3 are not, so the line differs in state from its control, which confounds every metabolic comparison in it. The progenitor line also differs in state from its control (radial-glia markers lower), which confounds every metabolic comparison in it.

disease_assertions.note: The only human WWOX-deficient transcript datum in which PDK is HIGHER; the two human neural transcript systems give PDK1 lower in sign only (inside the single-gene null). The isoform is unspecified in the sentence quoted, but the paper's Methods qPCR list names PDK1. Results name this condition (normoxia and normoglycaemia); the Discussion says PDK mRNA also rose in hypoxia-hyperglycaemia while the Results list for that condition names only PFK1 and PKM2 (internal inconsistency not resolved). n of the qPCR panel not stated in the sentence read. The PDK transcript sign therefore differs between a non-neural human line (up) and two neural transcript systems (not higher, lower only in sign): a cell-type contrast that is confounded (line, method, depth of silencing) and is not a finding about WWOX.

disease_assertions.endpoint: colorimetric PDH activity assay, knockout against control, four oxygen by glucose conditions
disease_assertions.locator: files/fulltext/PMID35328751_Baryla2022_PMC.xml, Results (normoxia and normoglycaemia): 'the activities of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK) and citrate synthase (CS) were not changed' (the sentence that carries the wording flag); Results (hypoxia and normoglycaemia): 'We didn't observed any significantly important differences in the activity of pyruvate [dehydrogenase]' (a different condition, quotation truncated in the source text read); Methods 4.10 names a PDH activity kit; Figure 5 caption: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase
disease_assertions.note: A null is NO_CHANGE, not proof of normal PDH regulation: n is not stated and PDH phosphorylation is not measured. Wording flag found in this cycle: one Results sentence lists 'pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK)' among the enzymes whose activity was unchanged, while Methods describe only a PDH kit and Figure 5b is labelled PDH; the repository reads it as the PDH assay (manifest entries 7 and 8); not resolved by the paper. PDH is named as unchanged in the normoxia-hyperglycaemia and hypoxia-normoglycaemia sentences; for hypoxia-hyperglycaemia the text says no effect on enzyme activities. In the same cells lactate was higher in all four conditions, hexokinase activity in two (normoxia and hypoxia, both with normoglycaemia) and LDH activity in two (normoxia with normoglycaemia and with hyperglycaemia); hexokinase is visibly lower in the knockout in normoxia with hyperglycaemia and citrate synthase lower in hypoxia with hyperglycaemia, both unmarked. The PDH point estimates in the knockout are higher, not lower (about 30 percent in normoxia and 47 percent in hypoxia, with large error bars), so the PDH result is a low-power null; n is not stated. The hypoxia-hyperglycaemia 'no effect' coincides with no reduction of total WWOX by immunocytochemistry and mRNA, but control WWOX there already sits at the knockout level, and the fractionated blot does show WWOX depleted in that condition (Figure 6). WWOX overexpression lowers PDH activity in hypoxia (p < 0.001). The 'knockout' is a CRISPR guide pool with protein 8.5-fold and mRNA 3-fold lower, not a complete knockout, and the unresolved 'PDK' wording stays as stated above.
disease_assertions.source: Baryla 2022 (PMID 35328751), Figure 5b and Results; carried through needs NEED-PDH-PYRUVATE-AXIS observation O2; Results sentence re-read in this cycle

Transcript level in the text; the byte artefacts behind the receipt (HTML and PDF under files/fulltext) are not present in the root checkout today, only an abstract-stub XML, so the locator was not re-opened in this cycle (UNVERIFIABLE_SURFACE for the blind audit: the Pdk1 sentence was not seen by any reader in this cycle). Mouse, non-neural; PDH phosphorylation and activity not measured.
disease_assertions.source: the 2014 WWOX and HIF1alpha paper (PMID 25012504), Results on HIF1alpha target genes (the sentence on Pdk1)
disease_assertions.target_id: Pdk1 transcript, Wwox-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts

context.developmental_stage: P10 to P14 (AAV9 study); young postnatal (the 2014 paper)
context.disease_id: constitutive Wwox-null mouse

disease_assertions.endpoint: blood glucose concentration, Wwox-null against wild type
disease_assertions.locator: deepdive_manifests/PMID42422765.json entry 37; files/fulltext/PMID42422765_Obeid2026_PMC_r2.xml (Results on promoters; Figure 1 legend: glucose at P14); deepdive_manifests/PMID25012504.json entry 10 (Figure 1 as drawn: wild type about 130 against knockout about 10)
disease_assertions.note: Two laboratories, two ages, very different magnitudes (about 95 against 130 at P10 in one study; about 10 against 130 in the other, a Figure 1 reading carried from the manifest and not re-opened). Hypoglycaemia is rescued by a neuronal-promoter vector; strong ubiquitous promoters rescued it early only (the paper says the protection was not sustained at later stages); an oligodendrocyte promoter and the weak ubiquitous promoter did not (JATS text read), so it is not a purely peripheral readout. UNVERIFIABLE_SURFACE for the blind audit: both figure readings (about 95 against 130; about 10 against 130) are carried from manifests, and the sentence quoted from the 2014 abstract is a background statement about earlier work, not a result of that paper; but the null dies early, so the endpoint is survivor-conditioned and confounded with feeding, seizures and growth (NEED-SYSTEMIC-GLYCAEMIA-GROWTH).
disease_assertions.source: Obeid 2026 (PMID 42422765), AAV9 study: P10 untreated knockout about 95 against wild type about 130 (manifest figure attestation); abstract-level statement re-read in this cycle from the local JATS: neuronal-promoter vectors rescue hypoglycaemia; the 2014 WWOX and HIF1alpha paper, abstract: Wwox-deficient mice 'succumb to a lethal hypoglycemia early in life'

context.disease_id: human non-neural fibroblast line with WWOX knockout (not a DEE-specific neural system)
context.genotype: WWOX CRISPR/Cas9 lentiviral knockout, polyclonal (WWOX mRNA about 3-fold and protein about 8.5-fold lower) versus scrambled-sgRNA control

disease_assertions.endpoint: lactate concentration, knockout against control, four oxygen by glucose conditions
disease_assertions.locator: files/fulltext/PMID35328751_Baryla2022_PMC.xml, Results: hexokinase 1.6-fold, LDH 1.4-fold, lactate higher in the knockout line (normoxia normoglycaemia), lactate still higher in later conditions
disease_assertions.note: Non-neural. Together with DA-I01-004 this is a raised-lactate, unchanged-PDH-activity combination: supply-side glycolytic overflow fits it as well as PDH restraint.
disease_assertions.source: Baryla 2022 (PMID 35328751), Figure 5d and Results; Results sentence re-read in this cycle

context.disease_id: WWOX-related disorder, one reported patient

disease_assertions.endpoint: brain lactate level in one WWOX patient
disease_assertions.note: n = 1, confounded by a second variant. It is the only brain-level lactate datum and it points the opposite way from the cell-line rows; it limits any argument that a lactate-lowering lever has a brain lactate excess to act on.
disease_assertions.source: discovery_ledger_current DL-BIO-008 (one patient with a confounding second variant; the ledger records the source full text as read and tags the datum DATO; not re-verified here), carried through needs NEED-LACTATE-LDH observation O4

context.disease_id: enzyme assays and a congenital lactic acidosis indication (not WWOX)

drug_assertions.endpoint: pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase inhibition by dichloroacetate
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Curated PDK inhibitor. Among the measurements retrieved, three enzyme rows record no half-maximal inhibition (IC50 above 1 millimolar; CHEMBL1133665, CHEMBL1132309, CHEMBL1133733, which carry identical companion values and record no top concentration), other enzyme-level rows differ (EC50 180 micromolar, CHEMBL5370584; EC50 5.7 millimolar with 64.2 % inhibition at 10 millimolar, CHEMBL4308888; Kd above 1 millimolar, CHEMBL3813671; EC50 above 100 millimolar, CHEMBL4732185) and a fibroblast lactate-oxidation effect appears at a high micromolar concentration: weak in vitro. The repository's existing safety position (peripheral neuropathy, BLOCK-1) is unchanged by this card.
drug_assertions.source: ChEMBL curated mechanism and activity rows of CHEMBL306823; Open Targets (phase 3, congenital lactic acidosis); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: PDK activity (family target; rat enzyme assay) and lactate oxidation in human fibroblasts

context.disease_id: enzyme assay, not a disease

drug_assertions.endpoint: PDK2 inhibition by AZD7545 or VER-246608
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Research tool compounds; no CNS, paediatric or clinical datum retrieved. The symbol PDK1 in DGIdb returns PDPK1 agents (collision documented in target_resolution.tsv); only PDK2-4 rows and UniProt-keyed ChEMBL rows are used.
drug_assertions.source: DGIdb (Drug Repurposing Hub, Guide to Pharmacology) and ChEMBL activity rows of CHEMBL3392645; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

context.disease_id: pilocarpine status epilepticus mouse epilepsy model, chronic stage (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
context.genotype: mice without pilocarpine status epilepticus as controls (strain not stated in the abstract)

drug_assertions.endpoint: PDH activity in the chronic stage of the pilocarpine mouse model, DCA against vehicle
drug_assertions.locator: PubMed and Europe PMC abstract (closed access, no open copy): PDH activity reduced by 65% against healthy mice in the epileptic stage, 'partially alleviated with DCA treatment'; PDH protein down 37%, Ser300 phosphorylation up 52%, not significantly changed by DCA
drug_assertions.note: PDH activity was 65 percent lower in chronic-stage pilocarpine mice than in non-epileptic mice and the drug partly alleviated this (significance not stated). In epileptic mice Ser300 phosphorylation was 52 percent higher and PDH protein 37 percent lower than in non-epileptic mice, and neither changed significantly with the drug. Two daily doses were tested, but the abstract does not say which was used for these assays and does not name the tissue. Total PDH protein fell 23 percent in non-epileptic mice on treatment, which the authors offer as a possible reason for the slight pro-convulsant signal.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, mouse, Durie 2018 (PMID 29913407), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

context.disease_id: acute chemoconvulsant seizure test (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
context.genotype: mice (strain not stated in the abstract)

drug_assertions.endpoint: latency to seizure, DCA against vehicle, acute test
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: 'DCA treatment did not increase latencies to seizures in the acute flurothyl seizure test'
drug_assertions.note: Chronic treatment (timing relative to the test not stated) did not increase flurothyl latency; two doses were tested and the abstract does not say whether the null held at both, and gives no effect size; in the same paper the drug was slightly pro-convulsant in the 6 Hz test. PDH engagement is reported for the chronic-stage pilocarpine mice, not for these animals. One laboratory.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, mouse, Durie 2018 (PMID 29913407), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

context.disease_id: acute electrical seizure test (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
context.genotype: mice (strain not stated in the abstract)

drug_assertions.endpoint: seizure outcome in the 6 Hz test, DCA against vehicle
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: 'slightly proconvulsant in the 6 Hz test'
drug_assertions.note: A small pro-convulsant signal in one test, read from the abstract only; the magnitude and statistics are not available.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, mouse, Durie 2018 (PMID 29913407), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

context.disease_id: pilocarpine status epilepticus mouse epilepsy model, chronic stage (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)
context.genotype: mice (strain not stated in the abstract)

drug_assertions.endpoint: latency to seizure, DCA against vehicle in mice with prior status epilepticus
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: latencies were decreased in status-epilepticus against no-status-epilepticus mice and 'were not restored by DCA'; conclusion 'DCA did not have any anti-convulsant effects in the tested models'
drug_assertions.note: A primary seizure-endpoint test of a PDK inhibitor in a model in which PDH activity is documented to be reduced; second-hit latency was shorter in epileptic than in non-epileptic mice and DCA did not restore it; PDH activity was reported as partially alleviated (significance not stated) while Ser300 phosphorylation and PDH protein were not significantly changed, so engagement at the second-hit test is unclear; the abstract does not say whether the same animals were assayed. Abstract level; the full text is not held.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, mouse, Durie 2018 (PMID 29913407), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: seizure latency (second-hit flurothyl test in chronic epileptic mice)

context.disease_id: lithium-pilocarpine seizure in adult rats, treatment started after the seizure (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: NeuN-positive neurons one week after seizure, DCA plus pyruvate against vehicle
drug_assertions.locator: files/fulltext/PMID36432491_Lee2022_PMC_r2.xml, Results 3.1 to 3.6; map record N-08 notes that each agent alone did not protect neurons; in the text read this is a Discussion statement citing earlier work (the design had single-agent arms; the figure was not read)
drug_assertions.note: Endpoint is histological neuronal survival, not seizure frequency or severity. After seizure PDK2 was higher (83%), PDH lower (62%) and Ser293-phosphorylated PDH higher (62%) in the seizure group: the PDK-PDH restraint is present after chemoconvulsant status epilepticus in this model (seizure, status-epilepticus injury, neuron loss and drug exposure are not separable), in wild-type animals; PDH is measured as protein and phospho-protein level one week out, not activity. Sample sizes differ between Methods and figure legends; western blots n = 3; immunofluorescence on 5 cells per section; one laboratory.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate combined with pyruvate, rat, Lee 2022 (PMID 36432491), body partly read; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: hippocampal neuronal survival after pilocarpine seizure

context.disease_id: congenital lactic acidosis in children, heterogeneous (pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, respiratory-chain defects, mitochondrial DNA mutation) (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: Global Assessment of Treatment Efficacy and linear growth over 6 months, DCA against placebo
drug_assertions.locator: PubMed abstract: no significant differences in the global assessment, linear growth, or frequency and severity of intercurrent illness
drug_assertions.note: A population in which lactate was persistently or intermittently raised, with a defined defect (pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency in 11, respiratory chain in 25, mitochondrial DNA in 7 of 43), aged 0.9 to 19 years; the drug blunted the postprandial lactate rise and still did not change the clinical outcomes measured over six months. Heterogeneous and short; the abstract reports no PDH-only subgroup, so a null in this design does not exclude a benefit in a defined genotype.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, human children, Stacpoole 2006 (PMID 16651305), randomized double-blind trial (43 patients), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: clinical global assessment, linear growth (children with congenital lactic acidosis)

context.cell_type: blood; cerebrospinal fluid in the long-term study
context.disease_id: congenital lactic acidosis in children (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: meal-induced rise in blood lactate, DCA against placebo
drug_assertions.locator: PubMed abstract: 'DCA significantly decreased the rise in blood lactate caused by carbohydrate feeding'; the 2008 long-term abstract adds that median cerebrospinal fluid lactate decreased over time
drug_assertions.note: Target engagement is shown in blood and, in the long-term open-label follow-up (Stacpoole 2008, PMID 18411236, abstract), in cerebrospinal fluid: cerebrospinal fluid lactate fell, but the drug level in cerebrospinal fluid was not measured, so CNS exposure stays UNKNOWN. Engagement did not translate into the clinical endpoints of DR-I01-006.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, human children, Stacpoole 2006 (PMID 16651305), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: blood lactate after a carbohydrate meal (children with congenital lactic acidosis)

context.disease_id: MELAS with the A3243G mutation (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: onset or worsening of peripheral neuropathy leading to discontinuation, DCA against placebo, crossover
drug_assertions.locator: PubMed abstract: 15 of 15 randomized to DCA taken off study medication against 4 of 15 on placebo; 17 of 19 discontinuations for onset or worsening of peripheral neuropathy; trial terminated early; global assessment not different
drug_assertions.note: The largest toxicity signal in the human trial record; the chronic paediatric cohort below saw conduction changes that did not become symptomatic (map N-08, Abdelmalak 2013, partial read). The two settings differ in age, genotype, exposure and follow-up, and they are not reconciled here.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, human, Kaufmann 2006 (PMID 16476929), randomized trial (30 patients), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: peripheral nerve function (adults and children with MELAS)

context.disease_id: congenital lactic acidosis in children, open-label long-term follow-up (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: conduction velocity and distal latency over years of treatment
drug_assertions.locator: PubMed abstract: conduction velocity decreased and distal latency increased in peroneal nerves; 'cannot be determined whether this is attributable mainly to the drug or to progression of underlying disease'; standardized height and weight declined slightly and stayed below the first percentile
drug_assertions.note: No comparator in the long-term phase; the underlying disease alone causes neuropathy. The same abstract records a 22% rise in 24-hour urinary oxalate.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, human children, Stacpoole 2008 (PMID 18411236), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: peroneal nerve conduction velocity (children with congenital lactic acidosis, long-term)

context.disease_id: diabetes mellitus and hyperlipoproteinaemia in adults (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: fasting hyperglycaemia after oral DCA for six to seven days
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: fasting hyperglycaemia reduced by an average of 24 percent; plasma lactate down 73 percent and alanine down 82 percent; plasma ketone bodies up 71 percent; cholesterol and triglyceride down; mild sedation in some
drug_assertions.note: Adults with raised glucose, a course of six to seven days; the abstract does not describe a comparator arm. The fall in lactate and alanine (gluconeogenic precursors) and the rise in ketone bodies are the metabolic signature that also links this lever to the ketogenic-diet question (card E04). The direction of the glucose effect when glucose is already low is the question, and this study cannot answer it.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, human adults, Stacpoole 1978 (PMID 625308), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: fasting plasma glucose (adults with diabetes mellitus or hyperlipoproteinaemia)

context.disease_id: endotoxaemic minipig, lactic acidosis with hypoglycaemia (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: plasma glucose and hepatic glucose output, DCA against untreated endotoxaemic animals
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: the progressive hypoglycaemia of the DCA group fell significantly below the endotoxin-only group (about 34 against 51 in the units printed) through lower hepatic gluconeogenesis and glucose output; lethality unaltered
drug_assertions.note: Acute infusion in a large animal, five treated animals. One of the settings in which a lactate-lowering lever made an existing hypoglycaemia deeper.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, minipig, Metabolic effects in endotoxemic minipigs 1986 (PMID 3521930), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: blood glucose in endotoxaemia (hepatic glucose output)

context.disease_id: cecal ligation and puncture sepsis in mice (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: blood glucose, DCA against untreated septic mice
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: DCA 'reversed sepsis-induced anorexia, energy imbalance, inflammation, dyslipidemia, hypoglycemia, and glycine deficiency'
drug_assertions.note: The only reversal in the glucose set, in a state that is NOT comparable to the minipig: in the open text plasma glucose and lactate (and pyruvate) were LOWER in septic mice, the authors acknowledge a fasting confound, and the same treatment reversed anorexia, so the reversal may follow feeding rather than hepatic glucose output. The comparability premise used in the first version of this card was wrong and is withdrawn.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, mouse, sepsis model 2022 (PMID 35730570), abstract (open access); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

context.disease_id: end-stage cirrhosis, 7 patients and 6 healthy volunteers (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: glucose production by isotope dilution and plasma glucose after intravenous DCA, cirrhotic and healthy subjects
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: DCA decreased plasma lactate by about 50 percent, glucose production by 7 to 9 percent and plasma glucose by 9 to 14 percent in both subjects with cirrhosis and control subjects; the decreases did not differ between groups (the null is the group difference); clearance about a third of controls
drug_assertions.note: Acute single infusion in 7 adults with cirrhosis and 6 healthy volunteers: a modest fall in glucose production and plasma glucose in BOTH groups; the only null is cirrhosis against control. Isotope-dilution human glucose kinetics, adult, acute; it does not transfer to a hypoglycaemic infant-stage brain-disease model, and it shows the lever lowering glucose in people who were not hypoglycaemic.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, human adults, Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in cirrhosis 1999 (PMID 10546922), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

context.disease_id: primary fibroblasts from patients with PDC-E1 mutations and five healthy subjects (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE)

drug_assertions.endpoint: average glycolysis with and without DCA, patient against control cells (lactate production was also measured)
drug_assertions.locator: abstract: in pyruvate dehydrogenase complex-deficient cells DCA decreased average glycolysis by 29%, with no significant effect on control cells, and lactate production did not change in either cell type
drug_assertions.note: DCA shifted flux in all cells, controls included, away from anaplerotic-related pathways (a 40 percent decrease) toward the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, and decreased modelled average glycolysis by 29 percent in patient cells (one of six patient lines, with an unusual splicing mutation, excluded from the average) with no significant effect in the control cells of five healthy subjects; untreated patient cells (excluding the same splicing-mutation line) had higher glucose consumption and lactate production than controls. Lactate production and NTP/NDP did not change in either cell type, so the DECREASE code is glycolysis only; no genotype-by-DCA interaction test is reported. It is a precedent for a glycolysis-lowering responder phenotype. A genotype-by-inhibitor interaction on glucose-derived acetyl-CoA flux is the repository's proposed discriminating experiment, not a result of this abstract.
drug_assertions.source: dichloroacetate, human fibroblasts, Simpson 2006 (PMID 16765624), abstract; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: glycolytic flux and lactate production in cultured fibroblasts

evidence_against: Three exploratory transcript tests in the one knockout organoid dataset are negative for the chain.
The paper does not name dichloroacetate or any PDH/PDK element.

IT7 P3/P1 (exploratory, independently verified): the six-gene glycolysis/lactate module was inconclusive in an independent WWOX-loss contrast (P47T hippocampus, p 0.060, inside its null; PDK1 lower by -0.08) and the network routes showed no added value for ranking compounds (signature route: not detected, not excluded); this card's compound was outside that comparison by design. A computational result, not efficacy data.

IT12 P1-alt (dated 2026-10-31; GSE298081, the authors' Data S4 read at the source; one WWOX-null HAP1 clone, no replicate or rescue arm, WWOX loss has no fitness phenotype in that line, the paper never mentions WWOX; association table only, not developed): loss of PDHA1 (qGI +0.567, FDR 0.020), CS (+0.566, 0.036), LIPT1 (+0.345, 0.075) and NDUFAF1 (+0.318, 0.051) is better tolerated by the null clone than expected, the opposite sign to a PDH-activation rationale. The four genes are common positive-interaction hubs (same-sign calls in 30 to 40 of 298 query screens), the system is a leukaemia-derived line and the endpoint is proliferation. Counter-evidence of low weight; the assessment does not change. Suggested probe: a PDHA1 knockdown arm in the isogenic PDH-activity experiment already specified.

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: qualified by several curated cards: P4-E-03; P4-I-01
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
not_known: Whether PDH activity or pyruvate oxidation is altered in any WWOX-deficient human neural system.
Whether pyruvate was tested in the fly metabolomics (MTBLS12344 not publicly retrievable).
Whether the Ldh rise diverts pyruvate from oxidation at all.

Whether any organoid transcript difference or null on this card (deposit GSE156243) is independent of the CRISPR clone and of the batch: the sequenced knockout organoids are four of ONE clone (1B, from edit-spanning reads, ADV-244, SCI, 2026-11-25), the other clone (A2) was not sequenced, the comparator is two organoids of the parental line (the authors removed two of four wild-type libraries, one for failed quality control and one for not clustering), and the organoids appear to come from one batch (the authors' Methods: organoids from the same batch were used for all analyses unless stated otherwise; their reply to reviewers speaks of the batch of the RNA-seq; not stated as a measured fact for these six libraries), so a difference here is not shown to be a property of the knockout rather than of the clone or the batch. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-244]

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

against: The study measured nothing in this branch.
PDK1 transcript is down and the PDK/PDH set is not different from chance in the human knockout organoid (exploratory transcripts).
The sima:GFP reporter (the authors' HIF1alpha homologue) is unchanged in one genotype pair; the authors name Atf4 rather than sima as primarily responsible.
Known neurotoxicity concern for the main compound; the ketogenic hypothesis dominates it on safety.

IT7 P3/P1 (exploratory, independently verified): the six-gene glycolysis/lactate module was inconclusive in an independent WWOX-loss contrast (P47T hippocampus, p 0.060, inside its null; PDK1 lower by -0.08) and the network routes showed no added value for ranking compounds (signature route: not detected, not excluded); this card's compound was outside that comparison by design. A computational result, not efficacy data.

IT12 P1-alt (dated 2026-10-31; GSE298081, the authors' Data S4 read at the source; one WWOX-null HAP1 clone, no replicate or rescue arm, WWOX loss has no fitness phenotype in that line, the paper never mentions WWOX; association table only, not developed): loss of PDHA1 (qGI +0.567, FDR 0.020), CS (+0.566, 0.036), LIPT1 (+0.345, 0.075) and NDUFAF1 (+0.318, 0.051) is better tolerated by the null clone than expected, the opposite sign to a PDH-activation rationale. The four genes are common positive-interaction hubs (same-sign calls in 30 to 40 of 298 query screens), the system is a leukaemia-derived line and the endpoint is proliferation. Counter-evidence of low weight; the assessment does not change. Suggested probe: a PDHA1 knockdown arm in the isogenic PDH-activity experiment already specified.
for: The Lucas-Clarke Ldh rise is the kind of change that could draw pyruvate away from oxidation (logic only).
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: No datum from any WWOX system at the activity or flux level.

p4_card.identity: Dichloroacetate (PDK inhibitor, phase 3 per Open Targets for congenital lactic acidosis, no US label found) and research PDK inhibitors (AZD7545, VER-246608). Devimistat is NOT counted: DGIdb gives it no action type on PDK2-4.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a pyruvate-oxidation block exists in WWOX-deficient neural cells. Nothing in the Lucas-Clarke study tests that; the branch logic (a raised Ldh pulls pyruvate away from oxidation) is indirect by two steps.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: PDK1-4 (HGNC:8809-8812; UniProt Q15118, Q15119, Q15120, Q16654), NOT PDPK1 (HGNC:8816); direction: release PDH from inhibitory phosphorylation; context: no WWOX system.
p4_card.next_measurement: IT7 P6 2026-10-29: the decisive measurement is unchanged and is specified in card I01 (PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation, activity and tracer, genotype by inhibitor); read PDK1, LDHA, LDHB, HK2, SLC2A1 and BNIP3 transcripts beside it; no computational ranking selects the compound arm. IT8 P3 2026-10-29, restated IT9 P4a 2026-10-30: a nanomolar inhibitor is added alongside dichloroacetate for the genotype-by-inhibitor arm (see card I01). The same discriminating assay as the ketogenic hypothesis, one step finer: PDH activity and labelled-glucose fate in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells. If PDH activity and pyruvate fate are normal, HYP-20260709-05 stays parked with a stronger negative; if pyruvate oxidation is blocked, this card and the ketogenic hypothesis are both reopened.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NOT NEW: HYP-20260709-05 and N-08 already hold this candidate (parked; dominated by the ketogenic hypothesis; peripheral-neuropathy flag).
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pharmacology: Dichloroacetate: weak in the retrieved enzyme and cell assays; no label found; spontaneous-report counts exist but are not rates. Research PDK inhibitors: enzyme tools only. Added class-level facts, no dose, no score, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE [IT59 2026-11-20 third packet change] (HE ADV-098 batch 8, database rows): dichloroacetic acid acts at millimolar concentrations in most measured rows read (four are sub-millimolar: PDK2 at 0.50 and PDK4 at 0.73 millimolar in the 2017 document below, PDK4 at 0.108 millimolar in a 2025 one, and a fibroblast EC50 of 100 micromolar). Within ONE 2017 document (an enzyme-linked assay on full-length PDHA1 as substrate, 30 minutes; four assays of the same design) the IC50 is 1.03 millimolar for PDK1, 0.50 for PDK2, 5.56 for PDK3 and 0.73 for PDK4: an eleven-fold range across the four isozymes within that document, PDK3 the least inhibited there. Other documents disagree: a second 2017 enzyme-linked document (tagged enzyme expressed in insect cells, 1 hour) gives PDK1 5.1 and PDK2 9.0 millimolar, the reverse PDK1 to PDK2 order, and carries no PDK3 or PDK4 value; a 2025 radiometric document gives PDK1 3.66 and PDK4 0.108 millimolar, with PDK2 and PDK3 only as bounds above 5. So PDK4 runs from 0.108 millimolar (2025 radiometric assay) to 0.73 (2017 enzyme-linked assay); the full isozyme order differs by document and assay because the place of PDK2 changes, so it is not read as a property of the compound; a lower IC50 for PDK4 than for PDK1, and for PDK1 than for PDK3, recurs in the first 2017 and the 2025 documents (two documents only, the 2025 PDK3 value a bound); no held document shows dichloroacetate inhibiting PDK3 better than another isozyme; two 2023 rows against PDK1 are bounds only (above 100 and above 50 micromolar), and a porcine PDK activation row is a bound above 100 micromolar; the database flags the 1999 PDK bound and the 2017 and 2025 PDK values as outside its typical range. A 1999 row gives only a bound, above 2 millimolar against PDK in vitro; an EC50 of 100 micromolar in normal human dermal fibroblasts is a different readout, with no order read between it and these. Five blood-cancer cell-line rows give 8 to 14 millimolar (MTT cytotoxicity, 48 hours, 2016). Separately, and not from these potencies: Pdk3 is not higher in two held mouse Wwox-deficient tissues of one study (the 1.55 times of GSE156243, a CPM ratio, 4 against 2 libraries, is not replicated in these mouse tissues and rests on one deposit; the mouse arms are not a like-for-like test of the human organoid), so there is no evidence here for weighting PDK3 as the relevant isoform in this genotype class, and none for excluding it as a target. No brain concentration of dichloroacetate in mice and no juvenile exposure were found (the rat brain PDK distribution paper of 1984 and a rat GSTZ1 paper are by title only; one neonatal query found no record); the openFDA label route returned no match for dichloroacetic acid, a statement about that route and not about development status.
question_history: IT7 P6 (2026-10-29): the six-gene module did not transfer decisively to an independent WWOX-loss contrast and the network routes showed no added value and the signature route was not detected, not excluded (loop_demonstration_it7_p6_20261029/README.md; P3 numbers independently verified). Status, F/C/P position and the premise are unchanged.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked PDH readout that a PDK inhibitor moves: PDH activity with phosphorylation at all three E1 sites and activity before and after dephosphorylation, and pyruvate fate (labelled glucose into acetyl-CoA, citrate, lactate) in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells; only then a functional endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX at the activity level. The Lucas-Clarke study reports no pyruvate (omics: top 200 variance features; the supplement lists significant metabolites only; detection not established), PDH, PDK or flux. In the human knockout organoid PDK1 is lower in sign only (inside the single-gene null, p about 0.30; not a demonstrated decrease), the PDK/PDH set is not different from chance and the LDH-to-PDH ratio is not shifted (transcripts).
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly study with no measurement in this branch; transcripts from one organoid deposit; compound statements are database rows.

cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: none measured in WWOX-deficient human neurons at the activity level.
cellular_context.limits: The transcript negatives are exploratory and do not show PDH activity or lactate are normal; the HIF1A-to-PDK-to-PDH step is unmeasured in any WWOX-deficient human neural system.
cellular_context.target_expression: PDK isoforms are expressed in brain; the WWOX-dependent level is UNKNOWN.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked PDH readout that a PDK inhibitor moves: PDH activity with phosphorylation at all three E1 sites and activity before and after dephosphorylation, and pyruvate fate (labelled glucose into acetyl-CoA, citrate, lactate) in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells; only then a functional endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX at the activity level. The Lucas-Clarke study reports no pyruvate (omics: top 200 variance features; the supplement lists significant metabolites only; detection not established), PDH, PDK or flux. In the human knockout organoid PDK1 is lower in sign only (inside the single-gene null, p about 0.30; not a demonstrated decrease), the PDK/PDH set is not different from chance and the LDH-to-PDH ratio is not shifted (transcripts).
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly study with no measurement in this branch; transcripts from one organoid deposit; compound statements are database rows.

abstention_card.an_abstention_is_a_result: The roadmap states it; this card names what would end it.
abstention_card.missing_datum: A baseline: no aberrant-to-normal transcript ratio exists for any WWOX splice allele in any tissue, no WWOX splice allele has had its RNA examined with an NMD inhibitor, and no intragenic precedent exists. Without a baseline an efficacy endpoint has no denominator.
abstention_card.search_record: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA, bounded to the set searched. 'antisense' and 'oligonucleotide' were 0 in the 20-record splice-relevant census set (19 of 20 read at abstract depth; known-roads § 2.8, 2026-10-20), not across every WWOX record: the repository holds WWOX papers that use an antisense construct (PMID 19366691) or a morpholino knockdown (PMID 25649963), neither a splice-switching correction arm. A later three-query PubMed leg with a passing positive control (analysis/splice_allele_rna_evidence_20260922.md) supports the absence of an aberrant-to-normal ratio; PubMed zeros are not re-runnable offline. Of the 20 records three measured a transcript from a splice allele.

candidate.name: Splice-switching ASO for a canonical acceptor allele

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried, and none may be derived from this card.

directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED means no matched comparison exists, which is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
NO_MATCH_FOUND is not 'does not exist'; NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA is not MAI_TENTATO.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED on every card: the bridge has no network and no pharmacological-label search was run. It is not NO_MATCH_FOUND.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; concentrations or exposures of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE at class level.

context.disease_id: WWOX-DEE, Q230P-class missense (reference genotype class)

disease_assertions.endpoint: WWOX protein detectable by Western blot (lysate fraction not separated)
disease_assertions.locator: CLAIM 019, paragraph 'DATO FUNZIONALE, CAUSA NON RISOLTA'; PAPER 041
disease_assertions.measured_result_note: Transcript comparable to reference lines, protein band not detected. One membrane, one exposure, one donor line, no healthy fibroblast control, no densitometry, no n. No proteasome inhibitor, chaperone, synthesis, solubility or half-life measurement exists; the authors leave open impaired translation or premature degradation. The endpoint is 'mRNA normal + protein not detected', not a post-translational mechanism.
disease_assertions.source: claim_registry_current CLAIM 019 (functional source: PAPER 041, a single-laboratory study)

context.disease_id: SLC6A1/GAT-1 variant (not WWOX)
context.species: human protein in HEK293 cells and Drosophila glia

drug_assertions.endpoint: variant protein expression and rescue
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: 4-phenylbutyrate (10 millimolar in HEK293 for 24 h; 1 millimolar in fly food for 48 h) rescued the fully ER-retained G443V and NOT the partly trafficked G443D; the rescued variants recover part of wild-type capacity with altered affinity (about 6 to 8 percent of untreated wild-type uptake in the single-concentration screen; Vmax about 39 percent for G443V with 4-phenylbutyrate and about 55 percent for G443D with glycerol, Km raised, Fig 4D,F); wild-type uptake was raised in HEK293 (clearly by 4-phenylbutyrate), wild-type fly expression was not. Glycerol 10 percent rescued G443D uptake and mature band in HEK293 (Fig 3B, 4D-E) and G443V uptake in HEK293 only (Fig 3C); uptake was not measured in flies, where glycerol and 4-phenylbutyrate both gave presynaptic G443V in imaging, glycerol's effect on G443V seizures was not significant, 4-phenylbutyrate reduced G443V seizures (Fig 6H) and did not change G443D seizures (Fig 6G). Bile-acid chaperones are not tested in this paper.
drug_assertions.source: Shah 2025 (R1 reading 40485335); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE

context.disease_id: several non-WWOX targets (Munc18-1, GAT-1, GABRA1)

drug_assertions.endpoint: wild-type protein abundance under the class
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: The earlier statement that the class raises wild-type protein in every target of the lot rests on four readings and is withdrawn pending a re-read of three of them (30266908, 42157447, 42587736). For the GAT-1 reading (Shah 2025, PMID 40485335): in HEK293 cells 4-phenylbutyrate and glycerol increased the wild-type hGAT-1 mature band per the paper's text (the representative blots show at most a modest change; not quantified) and 4-phenylbutyrate increased wild-type uptake (Fig 3A); in Drosophila astrocytes neither compound visibly changed wild-type hGAT-1 expression (single-section images, not quantified, Fig 6B), while 4-phenylbutyrate, with glycerol minor and unmarked, raised the retained variant G443V (about 14-fold in the text, about 9-fold by plot medians, Fig 6I, at least 10 brains per condition). The cell-line effect on wild-type protein is not shown to be variant-specific; the in vivo wild-type reading is qualitative.
drug_assertions.source: four R1 readings (30266908, 42157447, 42587736, 40485335); NOT WWOX EVIDENCE
drug_assertions.target_id: wild-type client protein of each target tested

context.disease_id: SLC6A1/GAT-1 variant (not WWOX)
context.species: human protein in HEK293 cells and Drosophila glia

drug_assertions.endpoint: functional rescue
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: MEASURED NO RESCUE (behaviour unchanged). Encoded NO_CHANGE: a reported null, not an unmeasured cell. In the same paper glycerol, an osmolyte-type chemical chaperone, did rescue G443D in vitro: the partly trafficked branch was outside the reach of 4-PBA, not of every chemical chaperone. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-281: the null arm is 4-PBA 1 millimolar for 48 h in G443D flies (Fig 6G, seizure behaviour unaltered); in G443D flies the transporter already shows a wild-type-like expression pattern (Fig 6C legend, Fig 6E, Supp Fig 4C), so the fly arm does not test a trafficking defect; 10 % glycerol was also not significant in G443D flies, so no tested chaperone rescued G443D in vivo; the same 4-PBA dose reduced seizures in G443V flies (Fig 6H); 4-PBA 10 millimolar also did not rescue G443D uptake in HEK293 cells (Fig 3B).]

drug_assertions.endpoint: movement deficit and ictal-like events
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: MEASURED NO RESCUE in null alleles, protein not measured (the authors could not assess stxbp1a or stxbp1b protein: no validated antibodies), bath concentration bounded by larval toxicity (text 25 and 50 micromolar, the Fig 1D legend says 10 and 25, the supplementary workbook writes 'mM'; wild-type survival about 70 percent at 50 micromolar, Fig 1C), assay separation of controls unestablished; movement was the endpoint on stxbp1a (stxbp1b movement also showed no effect), ictal-like events by local field potential on stxbp1b (nine larvae, 4-phenylbutyrate against baseline, unpaired t test on the same nine larvae, P = 0.8593, 95 percent CI -7.18 to 8.51 events per 15 min, so a large fall is not excluded); INCONCLUSIVE for a protein-expressing missense allele. Encoded NO_CHANGE.

drug_assertions.endpoint: total variant protein, class-I HDAC-inhibitor comparator (butyrate) at the same applied level
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Mutant total protein about equal to untreated control, no significance mark (three experiments; bar reading), at the same applied level as the phenylbutyrate class; the text lists only the phenylbutyrate class and two osmolytes as stabilising. On wild type the same comparator gave a scattered, unmarked value near 1.95. The comparator (butyric acid in ChEMBL) was more potent than the phenylbutyrate class on HDAC3 and HDAC8 in one ChEMBL document; on HDAC1 and HDAC2 the held table gives butyric acid two values (16 and 300 micromolar for HDAC1; 12 and 400 micromolar for HDAC2) that bracket the phenylbutyrate values (64 micromolar for the acid, 162 micromolar for the sodium salt), and which document carries which value is not resolvable from the held aggregate rows, so that premise is document-dependent. In the held ChEMBL table its HDAC6 value is only a lower bound, above 2 millimolar, a bound that lies below the 5 millimolar applied, so HDAC6 inhibition at that level is neither shown nor excluded; no HDAC engagement was measured in this paper, and no pan-HDAC or HDAC6-selective arm exists in it. A measured null in a cell that is not comparable.

drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Mutant total protein in Supplementary Figure 12a (HEK293T, three independent experiments): about 2.35 fold of control with trehalose and about 1.8 fold with sorbitol, both marked; Figure 12b (same cell line, same concentration) repeats the trehalose rise but shows about 1.0 fold, unmarked, for sorbitol, and the higher concentration of either gave no rise in panel a, so no sorbitol effect is established and the osmolyte arm for G544D rests on trehalose (sorbitol is marked for G544D in 12a and in yeast and for R406H and G544V in 12b, but not for G544D in 12b or in neurons) (corrected 2026-11-25, ADV-279; figure readings). Both were also raised in yeast by a second assay (panel c, fluorescence). The osmolytes act at high levels, so an osmotic effect is not separated from chaperoning; the effect is on wild type as well.

drug_assertions.endpoint: synaptotagmin-1 antibody uptake (function of the same protein), 4-phenylbutyrate arm
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Mutant total protein sits at about 4 to 8 percent of wild type in four of five variants and rises only about 1.05 to 1.65 fold with the class; the soluble fraction roughly doubles (soluble pool about 2 to 4 fold, reader arithmetic); function reaches or exceeds the untreated wild-type range for three of the four low-protein variants (R406H about 44 against about 55 does not with the class, and reaches about 58 with sorbitol; the fifth variant, P335L, has about 65 percent protein, an intermediate and not absent deficit, and its soluble fraction shows no marked change). The soluble-pool figures combine panels with different loading normalisers and carry a reader error of about plus or minus 10 percent of axis, and fold values near 1.05 are not separable from 1.0. Quantity and function are not proportional (read-out saturation not excluded; the authors report near-wild-type expression in neurons, not overexpression, and a pixel-threshold read-out); a steady-state deficit of about 12 to 25 fold is only about 1.5 to 3 fold explained by the measured turnover.

drug_assertions.endpoint: liver mutant enzyme protein and plasma phenylalanine (function read-out)
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Enzyme protein rose toward wild type with acetylated HSP90 up; plasma phenylalanine fell about 43 to 44 percent from sham at week 12 (44.1 from the printed group means, 749.41 against 1341.01; 42.9 from the mean of the three tabulated treated values, 765.9, against the two tabulated sham values) yet stayed about three times wild type; two sham animals against three treated; a higher dose caused abdominal oedema and deaths (that group was excluded from the analysis; kidney enlargement and ascites at necropsy); the tables list two sham animals although the Methods state three per group; no turnover measurement supports the authors' degradation reading. Suggests, in one small study (Pah enu2 F263S mice, two tabulated sham against three treated animals), that a mutant liver enzyme can respond to an HDAC6 inhibitor; this paper does not test whether butyrate engages HDAC6.
