mission_dimensions.route_note: qualified by one curated card: P4-A-01; Track is read only from the card(s) that state it - P4-A-01 state(s) a route and no Track (written before Track was qualified)

input.no_new_reading: Original cards: no paper was opened. IT5 P8 revision: the Munc18-1 paper's mutant panel of Supplementary Figure 12a, Figures 3 and 6 and the chemical-chaperone passages were re-read (a re-read receipt is staged under receipt_staging/scientist-b and is not yet in the ledger); HDAC potencies were pulled from ChEMBL keyless; the other sources are the repository's own receipted notes.
not_known: Where the Q230P protein is lost: never made, made and cleared, made and insoluble, made and epitope-invisible, or truncated. No fractionation, inhibitor, synthesis or half-life datum exists for the exact variant.

Whether any recovered Q230P protein would carry WWOX function: there is no per-molecule WWOX function assay in the repository, and protein quantity does not imply function (in the R1 lot quantity and function diverged in some systems and function could not be measured in others).

The share of destabilised-missense lesions that are stability lesions for a WWOX SDR-domain variant: the estimates carried in the literature are cited estimates, and the SDR-domain thermal stability is a missing measurement.
No drug has been given to any WWOX model carrying a missense or a splice allele (known-roads note, section 5).
Whether a cytosolic enzyme lesion behaves like the ER-retained branch at all.
Whether the class, if it acts, acts through chaperoning or through raising expression of the allele.
Whether the class acts on a soluble cytosolic mutant through HDAC6/HSP90 acetylation: butyrate does not engage HDAC6 and no pan-HDAC or HDAC6-selective arm exists in the soluble precedent.

The residual function of the Q230P-class protein per molecule and its amount relative to wild type: the reciprocal of their product is the fold gain any boost would need, and for Q230P neither factor has a calibrated value (protein not detected in one patient's fibroblasts with no detection limit stated, Johannsen 2018, PMID 29808465; function not measured), and the held P252A and P282A readings (over-expressed protein, Zhang 2025, PMID 41124647; for P252A also one cancer line, PMID 15266310) give no residual fraction.
Whether any function read-out of WWOX saturates below wild-type protein, as the soluble precedent's read-out appears to.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven separate queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the only synonym-driven record is one observational natural-history registry. Carried with the census's own caution: "A missing hit does not prove that no study exists." It answers seven queries against one registry on one date; unregistered, differently worded, non-NLM or later-registered studies are not excluded.

against: Wild type is raised in every target: the effect is not mutant-specific.
Not rescued: the partly trafficked G443D; null zebrafish (protein not measured); butyrate raised total immature protein with a small, variant-dependent function gain.
Mouse exposures were short (days); no brain exposure measured beside mutant protein; the human arm of one paper is one uncontrolled child.
No enzyme-class precedent for the class; the enzyme precedents use degradation blockade or an active-site binder.

The soluble precedent raises wild type as well, adds no enzyme, no route-inhibitor arm and no mRNA under treatment, uses a dominant-negative mechanism WWOX does not have, and its total-protein gain on four of five mutants is only about 1.05 to 1.65 fold.

A required-fold limit: a boost can at best multiply the mutant's residual function (amount relative to wild type times function per molecule), so parity with wild type needs a fold gain equal to the reciprocal of that product. No held measurement read for this card gives a calibrated value of it for Q230P, P252A or P282A. Q230P: WWOX protein was not detected by Western blot in one patient's fibroblasts, whose WWOX transcript level was almost identical to that of three other cell lines (Johannsen 2018, PMID 29808465; no healthy fibroblast control, no detection limit stated, function not measured). P252A and P282A (Zhang 2025, PMID 41124647; over-expressed Flag-tagged protein in thyroid-cancer lines): P252A protein is about 0.16 to 0.36 of wild type at steady state (Fig 4C-F), with about 0.3 of the starting level left at 6 to 10 hours against about 0.7 to 0.9 for wild type (Fig 4B), and chloroquine or ammonium chloride raise it about 1.8 to 2 fold (Fig 4D, 4E; function not read); P282A is about 0.6 to 0.95 of wild type (Fig 4C-F) and is a common population variant (gnomAD allele frequency about 0.07, Supplementary Table 4). Neither mutant differs significantly from empty vector in the function assays that include one (for example colony number relative to empty vector in CAL-62: wild type about 0.57, P252A about 1.3, P282A about 1.05, Fig 2B); growth, colony and invasion read-outs sit at about the vector level, while in some other read-outs the mutant mean lies between vector and wild type (gamma-H2AX, Fig 5B; NHEJ for P282A, Fig 5C; BCPAP migration, Fig 2F), so non-significance is not equivalence and none of this gives a residual fraction (no dose-response, over-expression). A patient homozygous for both had no WWOX nervous-system disease, and the authors suggest the proteins may keep some function (a conjecture, not a measurement). Separately, a liver-cancer line carrying a P252A change of unknown zygosity (SNU387) has low WWOX transcript and low protein, which cannot be attributed to the variant (Park 2004, PMID 15266310). The observed gains in the non-WWOX precedents read run from about 1.05 (a non-significant butyrate bar, DeLeeuw Fig 5F) to about 19 to 21 fold on the GAT-1 Fig 4G bars (by pixel about 6, 7, 14 and 21 for D52Y, V125M, A357V and G566H, the last two with 15 to 25 percent error because the untreated bars are 7 to 8 pixels high; by eye about 5, 7, 10 and 15), and to tens-fold or 14-fold where the untreated baseline is at the assay floor (Shah Fig 3B, glycerol on G443D; fly G443V with 4-phenylbutyrate). Wild type is raised in some precedents (about 1.2 to 2.7 fold) and not significantly changed in others (flies, Shah Fig 6B, image only; GAT-1 wild-type uptake with phenylbutyrate or TUDCA, DeLeeuw Fig 4A, bars about 1.2).

The measured turnover difference (about 1.5 to 3 fold) explains only a small part of a 12 to 25 fold steady-state deficit in the soluble precedent, so the 'made then cleared' branch is not the only candidate even where turnover is measured.
for: Allele-specific rescue of a fully ER-retained variant with protein and function read together (GAT-1 G443V, fly seizure-like episodes down).
Total and surface protein rise in other missense lesions with the class.

In the soluble cytosolic client (Guiberson 2018), phenylbutyrate raised the G544D mutant total protein about 1.8 fold (Supplementary Figure 12a) and about 1.5 fold (12b) and trehalose about 2.35 fold in both; sorbitol raised it in 12a (about 1.8 fold, marked) but carries no significance mark in 12b (about 1.0) or in neurons (Figure 6a, about 1.6); sodium butyrate, tested only on G544D and wild type in HEK293T (three experiments), did not raise G544D (about 1.0; wild type about 1.9, unmarked); with phenylbutyrate the soluble fraction rose about 1.7 to 2.4 fold in the four low-protein variants and the vesicle-recycling read-out was at or above the untreated wild-type range for three of the four (partial dissociation of quantity from function in the favourable direction; NOT WWOX EVIDENCE).
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Soluble monomeric client with a dominant-negative mechanism, or ER-retained membrane client, versus a recessive cytosolic SDR enzyme; CMV-promoter plasmid overexpression in cell lines, or lentiviral expression near wild-type level in neurons (authors' statement; saturation or excess not excluded), versus own promoter; wild type raised alike; the in vitro and in vivo gains are protein quantity, not WWOX function.

p4_card.expected_contribution: Function recovery of residual WWOX protein is the only contribution hypothesised; compensation, symptom and protection are not claimed. The branch (retained, cleared, insoluble) must be placed before any contribution can be stated.
p4_card.identity: 4-phenylbutyrate (and the related salt forms) and bile-acid chemical chaperones (e.g. the TUDCA class), taken together because TX-003 lists them together. The two are not interchangeable; the SLC6A1 reading found a similar variant-by-variant pattern only for the bile acid. Formulation relevant to any use: UNKNOWN.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WOREE (Q230P-class missense) as target. Origin contexts: STXBP1, SLC6A1, GABRA1 and GAT-1 variants in cells, worm, fly, zebrafish and mouse (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE). Bridge limit: one precedent of the lot is a soluble cytosolic client (Munc18-1) where the class raised the mutant, but no enzyme and no WWOX system was tested; wild type is raised as well.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: the folding or trafficking fate of a destabilised client; type of action debated among three non-exclusive classes: physical chemical chaperoning (the class and HDAC-free osmolytes both raised a soluble mutant), HDAC6/HSP90-linked acetylation (open for the class: the class engages HDAC6 at applied levels, butyrate does not, one cytosolic enzyme precedent responds to an HDAC6 lever), and class-I HDAC-mediated transcription of the cDNA (a class-I inhibitor did not reproduce the soluble mutant gain, a contrast that assumes butyrate is at least as strong as the class on class-I enzymes, which is document-dependent; promoter and mRNA-under-treatment controls absent). No source curates a chaperone target or potency for the class; its HDAC potencies are quantified at enzyme level and the applied levels sit well above them. Direction: up in protein; context: ER-retained membrane clients and one soluble cytosolic client.
p4_card.next_measurement: Build the wild-type function ruler first, then fate, then levers. (1) In an isogenic WWOX-null human neural system with one inducible promoter at one landing site, titrate wild-type WWOX across at least five levels and read a WWOX-dependent cell phenotype against measured per-cell protein (Tier 1: glucose uptake or lactate/oxygen consumption, which depends on WW1; Tier 2, binary confirmation only: neuronal Ca2+ firing; design in wwox_function_reference_it6_20261029.md) with antibody blot plus targeted mass spectrometry, soluble, pellet and total fractions, and transgene mRNA in the same wells, with empty/EGFP-null, WW1-dead (W44F/P47A) and isogenic uninduced wild-type arms, and L404A as an SDR-region binding probe only; (2) place the Q230P-class allele on that curve and read a per-molecule binding-competence ratio (WW1-dependent and SDR-region partners) beside it; (3) only then run the three-class lever panel of the IT5 P8 design (class-I HDAC inhibitor without HDAC6 activity; pan-HDAC or HDAC6-selective inhibitor; HDAC-free bile acid and osmolytes with an osmotic control), each also on the null line and on the wild-type ruler line, with the arm-outcome predictions registered in both directions. A result on the Tier 1 curve is read as recovery of the WW1-dependent axis only, not as rescue of SDR-domain function, unless an SDR-region readout also agrees. No abundance gain is read as rescue unless the variant plus compound arm moves along its own ruler curve with mRNA flat and the null line unaffected; a gain at equal protein above the variant's own curve is scored separately as a rise in per-molecule function. No WWOX catalytic activity is assumed or assayed: none is validated.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test in any WWOX system (registry-based, known-roads note section 2.8, 2026-10-20); no dedicated PubMed query for these molecules was run for this card. 4-PBA/TUDCA were carried as TX-003 and withdrawn on rationale (DIS-004), not on a result. NOT MAI_TENTATO-proof: unpublished individual experience is unreachable by any literature query.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pharmacology: Potency, relevant exposure and selectivity in a WWOX system: UNKNOWN. Re-examined in IT5 (pharmacology_it5_20261029/proteostasis_pba_a01.tsv): the only measured potency for the class is HDAC inhibition, at micromolar to sub-millimolar values (one HeLa extract study: low micromolar; recombinant enzymes: tens to hundreds of micromolar, with butyrate more potent than phenylbutyrate in the same assay and the order reversed in the HeLa study), while the cell experiments in the cited papers applied roughly half a millimolar to ten millimolar for a day (a toxicity ceiling at four millimolar in one paper) and the bile acid one hundred micromolar; so HDAC inhibition is quantitatively available at the concentrations used and cannot be excluded as the operating mechanism, and there is no numeric value for the chaperone mechanism of either compound, although qualitative active records exist for phenylbutyric acid alone (model-protein aggregation suppression and ER-stress cell protection, each at a single concentration and neither on a disease client); the bile acid has no folding or aggregation record In the sources: class not selective for the mutant; brain exposure not measured in any R1 paper. Keyless sources, IT5 P8 re-pull: no folding, binding or thermal-shift datum for the class or TUDCA in ChEMBL, GtoPdb or DGIdb (ChEMBL mechanism of record: ammonia scavenging for the sodium salt, Unknown for TUDCA; GtoPdb no curated interaction for either); in the two precedents analysed (applied at 2 and 5 millimolar) the levels were about 8 to 78 times the phenylbutyrate recombinant HDAC1 and HDAC6 IC50 (64, 162 and 240 micromolar; arithmetic, not occupancy); over the five applied-concentration rows of the table (0.5 to 10 millimolar; cells and, for 5 millimolar, a worm-plate level the table records as C. elegans) and all six held recombinant phenylbutyrate IC50 rows (HDAC1 twice, 2, 3, 6 and 8, 64 to 260 micromolar) the ratio is about 2 to 156, against the HeLa-extract Ki rows (2.8 and 6.3 micromolar) about 80 to 3,600, and a qualitative cell record at 0.1 millimolar in the same table would put the low end below 1 against the recombinant IC50 (about 0.4 against 260 micromolar); for butyrate on HDAC1 in the same two precedents the ratio is 6.7 to 312 (on HDAC6 only a bound); butyrate is 4 to 29 times more potent than the acid on class I in one document (its low values recur in another that lists no phenylbutyrate) but weaker on HDAC1 than the sodium salt in a third, so the relative class-I strength is document-dependent; butyrate does not engage HDAC6 in the one document that tests it.

SCI 2026-11-19 (R1, advisor_pilot_20261113/brainstorm_20261116/r1_conduction_endpoint_sci_20261119/R1_CONDUCTION_ENDPOINT_NOTE_SCI_20261119.md; mapped by IT): conduction in the Wwox-null brain was measured once (neuron-targeted deletion, acute slices P13 to P17, 8 slices from 5 animals against 8 from 6, graph-read N1 latency about 2.5 against 3.2 ms, N1/N2 ratio changed, Synapsin-Cre only, no rescue, no velocity, a control n identical to another experiment's n, Methods without a callosal protocol): a candidate readout that needs re-measurement with a rescue arm and animal-level statistics. Structural endpoints with demonstrated neuronal rescue exist (EM myelinated axons, CNP, MBP, CC1; g-ratio with a residual difference) and are the usable ones for an arm on this card.

Brain exposure of clemastine or of a thyromimetic in a Wwox-deficient pup, or in any neonatal or juvenile mouse: unknown (a total plasma value in the neonatal mouse was found for clemastine; none was found for the thyromimetics by the routes read, where papers on juvenile tiratricol dosing in Mct8-deficient mice exist with numbers not read; no neonatal brain concentration was found for either class) [IT59 2026-11-20 unit B packet change].

p4_card.identity: Pro-myelinating agents (muscarinic-antagonist class such as clemastine and benztropine, thyroid-hormone and antipsychotic routes) and, as a separate question, activity manipulation as a myelin lever. [ADV-001] For clemastine and benztropine two routes are documented (M1 genetics in culture; EBP inhibition with zymostenol accumulation in mouse OPC sterol profiling) and their attribution is unsettled; tamoxifen has documented EBP inhibition and quetiapine one main-text report of it; EBP is unmeasured for the other antimuscarinics named. A profile of the pathway intermediates per compound before target attribution is a design position (INFERENZA), not a result. This does not say that EBP explains the muscarinic route, that unmeasured compounds act through EBP, or that M1 is irrelevant (ebp_reannotation_adv001_20261113).
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF the Wwox-deficient oligodendrocyte lineage is itself the limiting compartment, which the neuron-versus-oligodendrocyte genetic arms argue against. Transfer unmeasured.
p4_card.mechanism: Target (if pursued): oligodendrocyte differentiation or the axon-oligodendrocyte activity signal. Direction wanted: more compact myelin. The causal compartment is neuronal, so a drug acting on oligodendrocytes alone is not expected to reach the cause.
p4_card.next_measurement: Wet-lab, not done: Wwox-null (or conditional neuronal) mice or co-cultures; arms: vehicle, chronic activity suppression, activity-raising manipulation, one pro-myelinating agent; controls: wild type with the same arms, neuronal-restoration positive control; endpoints: quantified MBP and g-ratio by electron microscopy, oligodendrocyte counts; discriminating result: the direction of the myelin change under suppression versus under activity.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: N-13 stands. New: the earlier record (DL-MECH-031 point 2) proposed that reducing seizure load might itself improve myelination because myelination is activity-dependent. The best-matched non-WWOX datum points the other way for a seizing network: Knowles 2022, Nat Neurosci (PMID 35501379, abstract read; absence-seizure models, not WWOX) reports that seizure-driven activity increases oligodendrogenesis and myelination in the seizure network, is prevented by seizure suppression, and that blocking activity-dependent myelination lowers seizure burden. The Wwox-null brain is hypomyelinated despite bursting, so neither simple sign is established. Also found: the 'near-complete MBP rescue' of the neuronal AAV is image-only (DA-W2-011).
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE if ever; broad recovery needs the developmental endpoint.
p4_card.pharmacology: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE, class level, no dose, no score, no compound carded [IT59 2026-11-20 unit B packet change]. CLEMASTINE (public-database rows of HE ADV-098 batch 6 and SCI's verified reading of primary papers): strong histamine H1 and muscarinic binding; within one document muscarinic M1 is the most potent of five subtypes with a six-fold range, an indication of M1 preference and not an identified selectivity; a second, undated panel measures M4, M5 and M3 (Ki about 3 to 8 nanomolar) and carries M1 and M2 rows without a value, so the M1 indication rests on the one 2020 document, where M5 is within 1.4-fold of M1; no measured myelination or oligodendrocyte-precursor differentiation row exists in the held IC50, Ki, Kd and EC50 rows (the link from M1 antagonism to differentiation is mechanism from the literature). Exposure: a total plasma Cmax of 44.0 ng/mL in the neonatal mouse at steady state of one daily oral regimen, dosed on the fumarate salt basis, that was not the lowest dose tested (Odell 2024, read at source by a blind verifier); no unbound and no brain value in that paper; juvenile rat brain detection is qualitative only (one paper, inconsistent about the age). Harm: in the healthy developing mouse, at the single higher dose described, slower conduction with fewer nodes, more differentiated cells and thinner myelin in thin axons (one dose only, so no margin can be read). Label (US label record, public database): clemastine fumarate syrup for allergic rhinitis, paediatric use confirmed from 6 to 12 years for that indication (labels in other countries differ). THYROMIMETICS: thyroid-hormone-receptor beta preference depends on the readout (sobetirome: seven of eight same-document pairs beta-preferring by 3.4- to 26-fold, one reversed; tiratricol: beta-preferring by about three-fold in binding and alpha-preferring in one reporter assay); the natural hormone's ratio of the alpha value to the beta value is 0.5 to 1.0 in the seven of sobetirome's eight same-document pairs that carry it (one has none), that is equal on both receptors or up to about two-fold more potent on alpha; no measured myelination row in those rows; papers exist on brain delivery of sobetirome prodrugs after systemic dosing in mice (the abstract gives no age) and on tiratricol brain content after intracerebroventricular delivery in Mct8-deficient mice (titles and abstracts read, numbers not read; a different disease context); a late start gave no myelination gain in one small mouse study of thyroid-hormone transporter deficiency, so the window may matter; label: tiratricol is authorised for peripheral thyrotoxicosis in MCT8 deficiency (a different disorder; nothing about myelination); none found for sobetirome. Added class-level facts, no compound carded, no dose, no score, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE [IT59 2026-11-20 third packet change] (HE ADV-098 batch 7, database rows and label records): four agents with four different mechanisms, so no potency comparison across them. None of the four has a database row that measures an oligodendrocyte-differentiation or myelination effect: the potency rows are the primary-target rows and are not the myelination mechanism (the link is literature; for the agents whose literature the sheet lists it was read at title level only). BENZTROPINE: muscarinic M1 Ki of 0.59 and 0.95 nanomolar at rat M1 (the 0.59 rows from rat brain membranes; the 0.95 row names no tissue) and 0.13 nanomolar in a human panel (up to about seven-fold between sources); pharmacokinetic and brain-distribution hits found by title for benztropine analogs only, none for benztropine itself by these routes; label: caution in paediatric patients over three years. MICONAZOLE: a human CYP51 IC50 of 200 nanomolar (lanosterol demethylase assay on enzyme expressed in a cell system, 2007) is among the rows; other human cytochromes (CYP3A4, CYP2C19) are inhibited at lower concentrations in several rows; the largest named human target groups are other cytochromes and a transporter; no row measures sterol intermediates or oligodendrocyte differentiation, so the proposed route from sterol-enzyme inhibition to differentiation is not tested in these rows; no rodent brain or plasma concentration found by the routes read; the label is a topical over-the-counter antifungal, which says nothing about CNS exposure. CLOBETASOL PROPIONATE (read separately from the parent record): glucocorticoid receptor IC50 3.17 nanomolar in rat liver cytosol against IC50 1.46 (Ki 0.66) nanomolar in a human panel (about two-fold on IC50; different species and sources); no rodent brain concentration of the plain compound found (central delivery is said to be a formulation problem by one paper read at title level only); label: topical, not recommended under 12 years. BEXAROTENE: within one 1997 document (human receptors) the RXR-beta, RXR-gamma and RXR-alpha Ki values (5.9, 8.3 and 16 nanomolar) against RAR-alpha, RAR-beta and RAR-gamma Ki values of 180, 50 and 130 nanomolar give an in vitro RXR preference of about three- to thirty-fold (about three- to eight-fold against RAR-beta), a comparable contrast within that document and not an in vivo selectivity; in the other held documents every RAR Ki or Kd is above one micromolar or is a bound (the lowest bound above 550 nanomolar), and one of them reports an RAR-alpha EC50 of 6 nanomolar against a Ki of about 5.5 micromolar, not reconciled; in that same 1999 document this RAR-alpha EC50 is also below its RXR EC50 values (20 to 28 nanomolar), with RAR-beta and RAR-gamma EC50 of 282 and 648 nanomolar, while its binding values favour RXR by about ninety-fold or more; two calorimetry rows elsewhere give an RXR-alpha Kd above one micromolar; other documents give human RXR-alpha EC50 from 2.7 to 149 nanomolar (measured values); a mouse plasma and brain quantification method paper exists (numbers not read); label: cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, paediatric safety and effectiveness not established.
p4_card.predictions: Registered: if hypomyelination is driven by loss of an axonal signal, an oligodendrocyte-directed compound leaves it unchanged in Wwox-deficient neurons and corrects it only after neuronal restoration; if activity raises myelin in this genotype, chronic suppression lowers MBP; if activity suppression helps, MBP rises. The three outcomes are separable by one chronic-suppression arm and one activity-raising arm against vehicle.

GRIN and rat rows are at the reading depth stated per row.
scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: One laboratory for every WWOX row used here; no independent replication.

p4_card.value_added: Records that the seizure-load-improves-myelin inference was an assumption with a counter-precedent, and that the neuronal rescue's myelin evidence is image-level.

cellular_context.limits: Myelin is measured as MBP image intensity; the treated-arm quantification does not exist.
cellular_context.target_expression: Oligodendrocyte-lineage markers SOX10 and OLIG1 are below 1 CPM in all six libraries of the week-15 organoid (4 knockout, 2 control), while PLP1 is 49 to 198 CPM (isoforms not resolved) and MBP about 1 to 4 CPM.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A myelin endpoint with a quantified treated arm in a Wwox-deficient system (MBP or g-ratio by electron microscopy, oligodendrocyte counts) after a pro-myelinating agent, after chronic activity suppression, and after an activity-raising manipulation, each against a Wwox-deficient vehicle arm.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: Neuron-specific, not oligodendrocyte-specific, Wwox loss reproduces the hypomyelination (genetic evidence of the earlier mouse work, PMID 33914858 manifest); neuronal gene replacement is reported to restore MBP by image. No pro-myelinating compound has been given to any Wwox system.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Mouse, early postnatal window; the AAV rescue works to the earliest days tested and later ages were not testable in the null.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Only IF the Wwox-deficient oligodendrocyte lineage is itself the limiting compartment, which the neuron-versus-oligodendrocyte genetic arms argue against. Transfer unmeasured.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: *importing a disease's dominant modality because the pathway diagram looks like that disease, without checking which way the arrow points.* CHAIN C reads like a tauopathy — WWOX loss → GSK3β de-repressed → pTau S396/S404 up (`CLAIM 035`, `DL-MECH-019`) — and tauopathy's dominant modality is **tau-lowering**. In the only system where the question was asked, tau-lowering **removes the benefit of bot

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried, and none may be derived from this card.

directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED means no matched comparison exists, which is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
NO_MATCH_FOUND is not 'does not exist'; NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA is not MAI_TENTATO.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED on every card: the bridge has no network and no pharmacological-label search was run. It is not NO_MATCH_FOUND.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; concentrations or exposures of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.
Every adjacent source is labelled NOT WWOX EVIDENCE at class level.

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: qualified by several curated cards: P4-C-01; P4-C-04; Track is read only from the card(s) that state it - P4-C-01 state(s) a route and no Track (written before Track was qualified)
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was opened for this card; the sources are the repository's own receipted notes and records.
not_known: Whether a missense or compound context with partial residual function would respond more, less or differently.
The upper bound of safe expression and any tumour risk.
Whether treatment after the earliest postnatal ages helps less, equally or more.
The shape of the dose relation between the two tested vector levels.
Whether the source's result is reproduced by an independent laboratory.

LIMIT on the electrographic readout of Obeid 2026 Figure 7, from SCI's measurement of the figure (PLAUSIBLE, not adopted) [IT59 2026-11-20 fourth packet change]: panel 7C shows two wild-type and three knockout points with p = 0.2000 on SCI's reading of the panel (the smallest exact two-sided value for 2 against 3), whereas the legend says n = 5 per group and the Results call the elevation significant: text and panel disagree and the disagreement is unresolved; panel 7E has 5 per group with per-animal values that do not overlap between knockout and wild type, pooled over a seven-day recording from about postnatal day 14, with the survivors per day not stated; whether panels 7B and 7C and panel 7E are the same animals is not stated.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (disease-models/wwox/research/drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven separate queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; the only synonym-driven record is one observational natural-history registry. Carried with the census's own caution: "A missing hit does not prove that no study exists." It answers seven queries against one registry on one date; unregistered, differently worded, non-NLM or later-registered studies are not excluded.

against: Not independently replicated within the repository; the source's mouse-versus-human construct comparison is an intra-study control, and the human-organoid source was not tested here.

SURVIVAL IS A STEP IN THESE DATA, BUT A STEP AND A STEEP CONTINUUM ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE: the lower level postpones death and reaches extinction; two dose points cannot locate a threshold; the adjudication in CLAIM 011 reads the step as strengthened, not established.
Body weight is equal at the two levels at one age and the weight comparison is survivor-conditioned on the lower side: an equality between unequal denominators is not evidence of grading.
Myelination dose relation never quantified; gliosis result binary against wild type with no untreated-null comparator; SWD has no low-level arm.
No tumour surveillance of any kind in a pro-apoptotic tumour suppressor delivered irreversibly; no measured ceiling.
Treatment age window tested only at the earliest postnatal ages; later NOT_MEASURED.
Behaviour at 3 months has no untreated-null arm by construction and a text-versus-panel conflict, not adjudicated.
for: SWD to a level not distinguishable from wild type in the strongest causal design of the corpus (blinded; single vector level).

p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WOREE (all genotypes carry some level of WWOX deficit) as target; origin: a constitutive-null mouse and human knockout and patient-derived organoids. Transfer to a Q230P-class missense or compound context is not established.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: WWOX gene dosage in neurons; type: replacement; direction: protein up; context: null mouse brain.
p4_card.next_measurement: An intermediate-level arm, defined as a fraction of the primary's higher level (never in absolute quantity), carried to 300 days with survival, weight, glycaemia, ECoG and quantified myelin in the same animals; and an independent replication. Either would change whether this is a threshold or a steep continuum. IT8 P5 addition (design only): a post-onset arm in patient or isogenic organoids, recording the same organoids at week 7 or 8, giving AAV9-WWOX or an AAV9 vector control at week 10 and re-recording at weeks 12, 16 and 24, severe and milder variant classes side by side, which supplies the missing same-organoid baseline, vector control and persistence.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Already studied (two mouse papers, one laboratory). A gene-therapy programme for WOREE is recorded at grant level (census § 3); that is not a registered study.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pharmacology: Not applicable in the small-molecule sense: biodistribution regionally uneven; potency, selectivity and CNS exposure of a human product: UNKNOWN. The absolute vector quantity is uncertain by exactly a factor of two in the source and no figure is reproduced.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: Early-window restoration of WWOX function (before the start of ECoG recording at about P14; phenotype onset never located) by neuron-directed replacement; the single useful endpoint carried is spike-wave discharge rate. Other measured families (survival, growth and glycaemia, motor score, myelination, gliosis) are in p4_card and are NOT compared by the bridge, which holds one disease assertion per packet. SWD rate is read after neonatal treatment of animals never recorded before it; it is a prevention or early-window readout. Spike-wave rate is an interictal network measure whose external precedent (other diseases, not WWOX evidence) is split.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: In the Wwox-null mouse, by one laboratory: SWD rate to wild-type level (single vector level); survival to 300 days at the higher vector level; a graded motor score; graded glycaemia at one age; WWOX protein graded; myelination qualitative only; gliosis binary against wild type with no untreated-null comparator in the quantified treated panels.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Constitutive null, not Q230P; one laboratory (the two papers share senior author and institution); no replication; earliest postnatal treatment ages only and NOT_MEASURED is not SMALLER; no tumour surveillance or overexpression-toxicity endpoint; SWD recorded over one week starting about two weeks after birth; threshold not located. Every endpoint is measured after neonatal treatment (P0 to P5) in animals that were never measured before treatment: the result is PREVENTION or EARLY-WINDOW, not recovery of a manifested deficit. No treated-after-onset arm exists; the authors state later intervention 'was not explored' and that this reflects 'model-specific biological constraints and technical limitations, rather than a definitive boundary'. External precedent now bears on this limit in both directions: a brain-directed vector replacing a missing protein in a short-lived null worked at P2 and not at P10, and its authors attribute the failure to transgene level and distribution; other nulls with short lives were treated later with a modest survival benefit (abstract level); a systemic capsid abolished established seizures in adults of a viable model. The perinatal window recorded here is not established as biological, and a null later arm would be uninterpretable without a measurement of the restoration achieved. These precedents are from other diseases (OTHER_DISEASE_PRECEDENT), not WWOX evidence, and change no window state.

disease_assertions.measured_result_note: Amplitude shifted up in knockout (cumulative distributions, KS test, taken here as on pooled events: the paper says only KS test on cumulative plots and the very small P values imply events as the unit; 10 cells per genotype from 4 wild-type, 5 heterozygote and 5 knockout animals); frequency is not different from the heterozygote but does differ from wild type (KS P about 2.4e-4; direction not stated in the text and not readable by eye from the curves); the heterozygote itself also differs from wild type in amplitude (P about 2.0e-4) and in frequency (P about 0.0018), so the frequency difference between knockout and wild type is shared with the heterozygote and cannot be assigned to complete loss specifically (with 4 wild-type animals, animal or litter differences are also possible); decay time constant not different, which the authors read as no overt change of the NMDAR:AMPA proportion. INFERENZA (the producer's, not the paper's): at the -70 mV holding potential NMDAR current is largely magnesium-blocked, so the recording is probably AMPAR-weighted; a residual NMDAR component is not excluded and no NMDAR current was measured. The incubation ACSF contains 1.3 millimolar MgSO4; the recording perfusate is not described separately. An NMDAR-dependent component is shown elsewhere in the paper (the delayed evoked field response is suppressed by d-APV, Supplementary Fig S3C, 6 slices from 3 animals); spontaneous excitatory currents are said to be 'isolated by voltage-clamping pyramidal neurons' at minus 70 millivolts with a K-gluconate pipette solution, and the miniature currents were recorded at the same potential with TTX added; for these whole-cell recordings no GABA-A, AMPA or NMDA antagonist is named (searched picrotoxin, bicuculline, gabazine, CNQX, NBQX, DNQX: none; d-APV appears only in the field-potential experiments). Loss of the target protein is not shown in this paper (the floxed allele and Cre line are cited; the knockout characterisation is in another paper), but an effect of the same manipulation in the same preparation is shown (the amplitude shift itself; sIPSC reduction in amplitude and frequency, Fig 4G-H, recorded in other cells: S-KO n 9 cells from 5 animals, with a high-chloride pipette solution). The text cites Fig 4C for amplitude where the legend assigns amplitude to 4B and frequency to 4C.

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Partial benefit / protection of function at best (network state); WWOX function stays lost. Variant-independent (Track A); Track B (missense class) unmeasured. Seizure or burst control is not developmental recovery (N-15).
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: W2 (scientist-c, 2026-10-27): no new full-text receipt; first-hand re-reads of already-receipted papers and of open PubMed Central text are described in the W2 record.
not_known: Whether NMDAR current, subunit composition or surface level is raised in any WWOX system.
Whether the raised mEPSC amplitude is AMPAR-mediated.
Whether a partial pore block reproduces the full block's effect on bursting.
Whether either drug affects maturation in a developing Wwox-deficient brain.
The GRIN2A variant class behind the burst-suppression association in the cohort abstract.

Whether the physiological NMDAR gate, extracellular Mg2+, can be raised enough to offset the knockout's depolarised resting potential and halved inhibitory current (see the IT6-P11 magnesium card and README in drug_repurposing/supplement_diet_it6_p11_20261029).

Whether slice exposure to perampanel is adequate: it is a noncompetitive AMPA/kainate antagonist with no effect on NMDA currents in culture and slow onset and offset (seconds), so exposure must be verified by the evoked response; the potency in the source is from submicromolar to just above one micromolar (a text-versus-figure conflict was withdrawn as a probable axis misread, inference), while a kinetic dissociation constant in the same paper is several-fold higher and is not reconciled there.

Whether any organoid transcript difference or null on this card (deposit GSE156243) is independent of the CRISPR clone and of the batch: the sequenced knockout organoids are four of ONE clone (1B, from edit-spanning reads, ADV-244, SCI, 2026-11-25), the other clone (A2) was not sequenced, the comparator is two organoids of the parental line (the authors removed two of four wild-type libraries, one for failed quality control and one for not clustering), and the organoids appear to come from one batch (the authors' Methods: organoids from the same batch were used for all analyses unless stated otherwise; their reply to reviewers speaks of the batch of the RNA-seq; not stated as a measured fact for these six libraries), so a difference here is not shown to be a property of the knockout rather than of the clone or the batch. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-244]

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. At best a reduction of a network state; no developmental benefit is implied.
p4_card.identity: Memantine (approved, uncompetitive NMDAR pore blocker; paediatric safety and effectiveness not established on its label) and perampanel (approved, non-competitive AMPAR antagonist; paediatric label for partial-onset seizures). Tool compounds: d-APV. Both are symptomatic-network levers on one measured phenotype, not WWOX restoration.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF the neuron-specific Wwox bursting phenotype is driven by a measurable gain in glutamatergic transmission that a partial block of NMDAR or AMPAR corrects without harming activity-dependent maturation. Transfer to the reference genotype is unmeasured for both alleles: the slice model is a Synapsin-Cre knockout, not a missense or splice allele.
p4_card.mechanism: Targets: NMDAR (GRIN1 with GRIN2A/2B/2D) and AMPAR (GRIA1-4). Direction wanted: lower excitatory gain. Context: juvenile neocortical slice, neuron-specific knockout. Memantine is a use-dependent pore blocker with subunit-dependent, assay-dependent potency; d-APV is a competitive full block: the tool result does not transfer quantitatively to the drug.
p4_card.next_measurement: Wet-lab, not done: Wwox-deficient versus parental or isogenic neurons or slices; graded memantine versus perampanel versus d-APV; controls: wild type, heterozygote, vehicle, washout, an NMDAR-selective and an AMPAR-selective evoked-current check to define which receptor is raised (NMDA:AMPA ratio under voltage control, not the mEPSC decay); endpoints: burst frequency, duration, amplitude, phase-amplitude coupling, then a maturation endpoint; discriminating result: a partial block that abolishes bursting in knockout and spares wild-type activity versus one that does not.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Memantine on the NMDAR node is already map record R-02 (class PROMISING_BUT_MECHANISTIC_GAP). New here: (1) the sign of the receptor lesion decides memantine's response in the one genetic-NMDAR cohort that stratified by function, so the 'GRIN2A corroborates the node' argument (DL-MECH-002) corroborates the node, not the sign; (2) the AMPAR arm, never carried as a node, rests on the only direct synaptic measurement in the knockout (raised mEPSC amplitude), and is untested. Coverage: PubMed searches of 2026-10-27 (GRIN-memantine, neonatal memantine, WWOX myelin), the Karnstedt full text, the repository's perampanel notes; NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA for any memantine or perampanel arm in a Wwox model, not MAI_TENTATO.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Memantine label: paediatric safety and effectiveness not established; two controlled paediatric autism studies failed. Perampanel label: partial-onset seizures from 4 years of age. Interactions and labelled warnings were NOT assessed (adapter sections lacked them). No paediatric suitability for WWOX-DEE is presumed.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A; Track B untested.
p4_card.pharmacology: Memantine: use-dependent channel blocker; recorded potency depends on voltage, magnesium and agonist level and spans several orders of magnitude across assays (README section 4). Perampanel: non-competitive AMPAR antagonist. CNS exposure for both is expected from their indications but is not verified here for the slice-relevant free fraction.
p4_card.predictions: Registered before any experiment: (a) if bursting reflects raised NMDAR function, a partial memantine exposure lowers burst frequency in knockout slices dose-dependently and not in wild type; (b) if it reflects raised AMPAR gain, perampanel does and memantine less; (c) if both are permissive routes of a network that recruits NMDAR, only the full block works and neither drug is a lever. Result (c) closes the strand.

abstention_card.missing_datum: A dose-by-timing series of Wnt/GSK3/CK1 modulation in a developing cortex with progenitor, layer-neuron and electrographic endpoints, in any WWOX system; and a measured activation step (reporter or nuclear/cytosolic beta-catenin). Two partial exceptions are in the repository: the CK1-alpha-inhibiting multikinase compound of the D01 card was given to knockout organoids (attribution among Wnt, MYC and CDK ambiguous), and a GSK3 inhibitor was given acutely to Wwox-null mice before a convulsant challenge with a seizure endpoint and a measured GSK3 phospho-state in brain (PMID 32000863, repository reading, text re-inspected); neither measures the activation step by reporter or beta-catenin. GSK-3 premise status after the 2026-11 comparison work (class level; hypothesis): the GSK-3 and Wnt transcript premise was not supported in the organoid and not distinguishable from random gene sets in the held postnatal day 17 mouse cortex (bulk, three against four animals; the Wnt sign agrees with the premise, inside the null band in the primary run and borderline in the blind recompute), and, among the partners in the held literature, one interactome partner, GSK3beta, meets the registered criteria with narrowings (directness not shown by the assays; the pharmacology of the criterion is partial, lithium at abstract level and no GSK3beta-specific non-lithium constant read in a primary source; the cell readout is a retinoic-acid-differentiated neuroblastoma line; the only tissue datum, lower phospho-Ser9 in Wwox-null brain, is the direction of more active kinase, whereas the cell-line paper reports phospho-Ser9 unchanged and attributes its effect to binding: the sources are in tension on the role of Ser9); no GSK-3 substrate measurement exists in a Wwox-deficient neuron (the cell-line paper reads Tau phospho-sites after WWOX knockdown and overexpression in a neuroblastoma line) [IT59 2026-11-20 packet change].

evidence_against: SPECIFICITY FAILED: lithium suppressed the provoked seizure in all three genotypes, wild type included (Figure 7d; entries 0, 22).

The causal attribution to GSK3beta rests on lithium alone; the paper's own Discussion names lithium's other documented actions, including Wnt/beta-catenin-dependent effects (entry 3). Lithium acts on many targets besides GSK3beta.

The only cell-line source (Wang 2012, PMID 22193544) reports Ser9 phosphorylation unchanged during retinoic-acid differentiation of SH-SY5Y cells, while WWOX rose (entry 5): that is a WWOX-gain, differentiation context, not a WWOX-loss measurement, and must not be read as a knockdown result; the knockdown experiment of that paper measured Tau phosphorylation (entry 8), not Ser9.
Direction conflict (INFERENZA): beta-catenin stabilisation by lithium would push an axis that is already raised in WWOX-loss organoids (map record R-04, axis M5; card P4-D-02).
Different control groups and schedules for lithium and ethosuximide inside one figure (entries 27, 28): the two drugs are not compared on equal terms.
A clinical anticonvulsant effect would be symptomatic: CLAIM 031 states that seizure control does not buy development.

input.no_new_reading: No paper was opened for this card. Every locator is an existing entry of the deep-dive manifests PMID32000863.json and PMID22193544.json; the figure statements are those entries' own.
not_known: Whether lithium does anything in a Wwox-deficient system that it does not do in a wild-type one (the one experiment that tested it answered no).
Whether lithium moves GSK3beta Ser9 phosphorylation or kinase activity in a Wwox-null brain: lithium's effect on the Ser9 readout was not measured in this system.

Whether GSK3beta abundance or Ser9 state tracks activity here: the sources are in tension and no kinase-activity assay exists in WWOX-deficient cells or tissue (the kinase assays of the cell-line paper are cell-free, with purified recombinant proteins, and show WWOX protein lowering GSK3beta-driven Tau phosphorylation in vitro). The cell-line paper reports phospho-Ser9 unchanged along a retinoic-acid time course while WWOX rises; no experiment in it manipulates WWOX and reads Ser9, and the phrase 'S9-independent' occurs nowhere in its text; the only tissue datum (Wwox-null brain, cerebellum, hippocampus and cortex; the legend says postnatal day 20 and the Methods say 14) reports LOWER phospho-Ser9, as a ratio to beta-actin, with representative results of four independent experiments and the number of animals not stated (registry CLAIM 035 Evidence boundary, BATCH_20261120_001; the earlier wording of this item, 'S9-independent inhibition', is withdrawn) [IT59 2026-11-20 packet change].
Whether the null-genotype hypersusceptibility is a driver of the developmental phenotype or an amplifier on a malformed brain (entry 6).
Whether the wild-type response is floor-limited in a way that hides a genotype difference.
Any allele-specific datum (Q230P class or splice allele): none exists for lithium.
Net direction on the Wnt axis: lithium stabilises beta-catenin, and WWOX-loss organoids show nuclear beta-catenin already raised (card P4-D-02).

mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
not_known: Whether a WWOX-deficient human neural cell has a measurable bioenergetic defect that a ketone substrate would bypass.
Whether lactate is raised, normal or low in WWOX-deficient human brain across ages and contexts.

In a held report of five paediatric WOREE patients (Chong 2023, PMID 36537114) epilepsy responded to a ketogenic diet in three (patients 1, 2 and 4); the lactate range of 2.4 to 3.3 mmol/L in one individual is a registry statement (ADV-259) not found in the held text (8 delivered chunks only; the case narratives of patients 1 to 4 are not held; searched 2026-11-26 for lactate, lactic and mmol); other held WOREE reports are less favourable; the Pdk1 transcript and serum-lactate datum in the Wwox-null MEF and mouse paper is non-neural and measures no PDH.

SCI 2026-11-19 (ADV-074, advisor_pilot_20261113/brainstorm_20261116/h_glucose_axis_adv074_sci_20261119/GLUCOSE_METABOLIC_AXIS_FIRST_PASS_ADV074_SCI_20261119.md; mapped by IT): the card's evidence is clinical and tiny with no metabolic readout in any WWOX-deficient neural system; on the held originals its rationale neither gains nor loses decisively: it would gain plausibility (an alternative brain fuel) only if hypoglycaemia or glucose use contributes to excitability, which nothing shows, and it would reduce to a generic anticonvulsant action if seizures occur with normal glucose (the P47T adults and the neuron-targeted line suggest they may). A diet that lowers blood glucose would act on pups that are already hypoglycaemic from about P10 and die: whether it helps or harms is unknown (a hypothesis-level caution, not advice). No change of tier.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

against: IT12 P1-alt caution (dated 2026-10-31; same screen, GSE298081, one unreplicated WWOX-null HAP1 clone, non-neural, proliferation endpoint, association only): loss of SLC2A1 (qGI -0.593, FDR 0.050) and HK2 (-0.464, 0.040) is worse tolerated by the null clone. A caution on direction for any glucose-restriction or 2-deoxyglucose-class idea, not evidence of harm in neurons.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: The fly lactate result is conditional on amyloid and cannot be used for or against the Warburg direction in WWOX-null neurons.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN beyond the empirical seizure-control use.
p4_card.identity: Ketogenic diet (HYP-20260709-01, map record R-05) and, as a direction control only, MCT1 blockade (AZD3965 in DGIdb). No new compound.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: A decision for the treating clinical team, not for this system; this card only records the consequence of the Lucas-Clarke reading: no direct support and no refutation.
p4_card.next_measurement: PDH-specific readouts in donor-derived WWOX-deficient cells or the existing knockout organoids against isogenic controls: PDH activity in a lysate that preserves phosphorylation, phospho-PDHA1 (Ser293, UniProt P08559 precursor numbering; Ser232 and Ser300 are also PDK sites), 13C-glucose or ketone tracing, pyruvate-to-lactate ratio, NADH/NAD+. Seahorse OCR/ECAR is a general screen of respiration and acidification, not a PDH measure, and a normal result in non-neural cells is non-significance, not equivalence; it is useful but not the only discriminating test (HYP-20260709-01, verification 2026-10-27).
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NOT NEW: existing hypothesis, updated with a consequence note on 2026-10-26.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.

scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Statements marked INFERENZA, including every statement about what a compound would do in WWOX-deficient tissue, are OWED a blind audit by another actor.
scope_of_checks.formal_checks: Disease-side fly rows carry verbatim locators in the manifest (104 entries; entries 31, 49, 89, 94 SUPPORTED by a blind audit, entry 95 narrowed after an OVERSHOOT finding); the compound statements are abstract-level and unaudited.
scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: No independent replication of any fly row is held; the organoid rows are one laboratory's deposit.

external_not_wwox_evidence: DGIdb SLC16A1 rows: AZD3965 (inhibitor), valproic acid and sodium butyrate (no action type)

p4_card.state_of_known_roads: HYP-20260709-01 (ranked, proposed-to-L9), R-05, DL-MECH-020, DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009.
p4_card.value_added: Records that this paper changes nothing for the ketogenic hypothesis and names the one measurement that still decides it.

cellular_context.limits: No metabolic readout of the lever exists in a WWOX-deficient human neural system; the lactate rows have opposite signs in the fly (with and without amyloid) and in one human MRS report.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: The existing minimal falsifier of HYP-20260709-01: Seahorse OCR/ECAR on donor-derived cells or the existing organoids; this card adds no new endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: The ketogenic diet in WWOX-DEE: tried in 3 patients in one cohort and continued in 1; a null-genotype report where it was suspended. The Lucas-Clarke study contains no diet, ketone, PDH or pyruvate arm.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: n of 3 and n of 1 clinical reports; fly lactate is amyloid-conditional.

disease_assertions.measured_result_note: Ratio 0.24, 0.29, 0.13, 0.14 in the four knockouts and 0.29, 0.30 in the two wild types: not higher in knockouts, so no transcript-level hint of a more depolarising chloride gradient; SLC12A2 is flat and SLC12A5 is higher in two knockouts. evidence_against: No transcript-level hint of a raised NKCC1:KCC2 ratio in the knockout organoid.
Poor CNS penetration is a known limitation.
Window may be closed.
No measurement of the premise.

IT13 P3a (2026-10-31): also no transcript support in the P17 Wwox-deletion mouse deposits (NKCC1:KCC2 ratio not raised in the three hippocampal contrasts, Slc12a5 higher in one; transcript only, 2 to 4 animals per arm; E_GABA unmeasured). [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-239: in the cortex deposit of the neuron-targeted deletion (4 control, 3 knockout libraries) the Slc12a2/Slc12a5 ratio is higher by 0.24 log2 with overlapping libraries, and this falls to 0.085 when one control library is removed; Slc12a5 itself is lower in all three knockout libraries than in all four controls (log2 -0.65); among the hippocampal contrasts Slc12a5 is higher only in the Nestin-Cre one (+0.28, overlapping) and lower in the Syn-Cre and germline-null ones (-0.55, -0.41).]

IT30 (non-WWOX, neonatal acquired-seizure models and trials; abstract or partial text, rows E03 E05 E07 E08 E09 E10 E11 E13 of the IT29 epilepsy package): the effect of NKCC1 blockade is state- and model-dependent, not a general property of the target. Recurrent seizures raise intracellular chloride, invert the GABA-A effect and bumetanide limits that accumulation (PMID 20810895, partial text; intact neonatal hippocampi, seizures induced in vitro; 187 cells from 4 hippocampi, ADV-276, 2026-11-25); in a hypoxia model bumetanide alone had little or no effect (PMID 23536761, partial text); two rat-pup asphyxia studies found no potentiation of phenobarbital, the second at a raised bumetanide exposure (PMID 33258158, then PMID 33955541, abstracts only). For balance, the same record holds favourable rows: a target-controlled slice effect (PMID 16227993), a phenobarbital combination that cut seizure incidence in the hypoxia model (PMID 23536761), and a non-NKCC1 analogue that did potentiate phenobarbital (PMID 33955541).

IT30 (human neonates with acquired seizures, not a genetic lesion): an open-label dose-finding trial was stopped early for limited seizure reduction and adverse reactions (PMID 25765333, abstract only); a small randomised pilot reported a greater post-dose reduction in the treated arm in a post-hoc analysis adjusted for a baseline imbalance and was not powered for efficacy (PMID 33201535, partial text). The two results disagree and neither addresses a Wwox-deficient lesion or development.

IT30: a hearing signal was reported after bumetanide add-on in neonates (PMID 25765333, abstract only), confounded by aminoglycoside co-exposure and the underlying injury; a pilot also reported a small imbalance with the same confounders (PMID 33201535). Unknown whether it is attributable to the drug: not a safety conclusion either way.

SCI 2026-11-18 (ADV-065c, after an independent verifier with full inputs; wording supplied by SCI and mapped here by IT, counter-evidence qualification only): the transcript panels are composition-confounded and descriptive (one pool per arm, hippocampal; six organoid libraries from one parental line); neuron-restricted values show no neuronal KCC2 transcript deficit and a lower neuronal NKCC1 transcript; transcript level did not predict E_GABA in two other models (Yuan 2019, Egawa 2023); uninformative for or against a depolarised gradient.

input.no_new_reading: W2 (scientist-c, 2026-10-27): no new full-text receipt; first-hand re-reads of already-receipted papers and of open PubMed Central text are described in the W2 record.
not_known: E_GABA in any Wwox system.
NKCC1 and KCC2 protein levels.
Human brain or CSF exposure of bumetanide (the mouse brain to plasma ratio is about 0.015 to 0.02, abstract level).

Whether the neonatal acquired-seizure record (state-dependent effect, discordant small trials) transfers to a genetic developmental epileptic encephalopathy: none of those preparations carries a Wwox deficiency; the chloride rise measured in one of them is seizure-induced (PMID 20810895; ADV-276, 2026-11-25: Clomeleon imaging in neonatal CLM-1 mice, 187 cells from 4 intact hippocampi under low-magnesium solution, mean +/- SE; in vitro), not measured in a genetic model.

Whether any organoid transcript difference or null on this card (deposit GSE156243) is independent of the CRISPR clone and of the batch: the sequenced knockout organoids are four of ONE clone (1B, from edit-spanning reads, ADV-244, SCI, 2026-11-25), the other clone (A2) was not sequenced, the comparator is two organoids of the parental line (the authors removed two of four wild-type libraries, one for failed quality control and one for not clustering), and the organoids appear to come from one batch (the authors' Methods: organoids from the same batch were used for all analyses unless stated otherwise; their reply to reviewers speaks of the batch of the RNA-seq; not stated as a measured fact for these six libraries), so a difference here is not shown to be a property of the knockout rather than of the clone or the batch. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-244]

Whether the hippocampal bulk contrasts on this card rest on independent animals: the arms are 2 or 3 libraries (GSE158681), one mouse per library is not stated in the sources read, and whether the same mice gave the cortices is not stated. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-247] Whatever a library contains it is at most one independent unit, so the library count is an upper bound on n; if a library is one mouse, the 2 control libraries cover at most 2 of the 4 control cortices, so the control hippocampi and cortices are not all the same mice. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-250]

p4_card.identity: Bumetanide (approved loop diuretic). Identity check 2026-10-27: ChEMBL_37 curates its mechanism as inhibition of the NKCC2 transporter only; NKCC1 appears in three activity rows (two single-concentration inhibition readings in HEK cells and one fitted value in HT-29 cells by rubidium uptake), so the NKCC1 target of the repurposing idea is an activity-table fact, not a curated mechanism.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF GABA is depolarising in Wwox-deficient neurons at the relevant age; unmeasured. The CNS penetration of bumetanide is a known limitation (map R-07).
p4_card.mechanism: Target NKCC1 (SLC12A2); wanted direction: lower intracellular chloride so GABA hyperpolarises; sign depends on an unmeasured quantity.
p4_card.next_measurement: Gramicidin perforated-patch E_GABA in Wwox-deficient versus parental neurons or slices at three ages (including the earliest culturable), NKCC1 and KCC2 protein by immunoblot or immunostaining, GABA puff response; controls: wild type and heterozygote, bicuculline or gabazine sensitivity, an NKCC1 knockdown arm in place of the drug; the compound is applied in the bath ex vivo, and a systemic response requires verification of relevant exposure (IT8 P3, restated IT9 P4a); discriminating result: a depolarised E_GABA specific to the knockout that an NKCC1 manipulation shifts.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Map R-07 stands as INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. New: (1) the transcript-level ratio in the public human knockout deposit does not point to a depolarising gradient (descriptive, confounded: the SLC12A2 to SLC12A5 transcript ratio is 0.13 to 0.29 in knockout against 0.29 to 0.30 in wild type, not higher, and clearly lower only in the two knockout libraries that also carry more of the inhibitory-neuron markers GAD1 and SLC32A1, both of which the authors' own list gives as higher in knockout. The deposit is GSE156243, four knockout and two wild-type organoid libraries at 15 weeks from one embryonic stem cell line, two further wild-type libraries having been excluded by the authors for quality. A second human knockout record, E-MTAB-14792, exists but returned 403 Study not accessible on 2026-10-25); (2) the target-identity note above; (3) the single experiment is written out with controls. Neonatal-seizure and autism trials exist (titles retrieved: NEMO open-label dose-finding in newborn hypoxic-ischaemic seizures, PMID 25765333; a phase 3 autism programme, PMID 35292925; a phase 2 autism trial, PMID 32730977); their abstracts (PubMed, read 2026-11-26) report that NEMO was stopped early for serious adverse reactions and limited evidence of seizure reduction (hearing impairment in 3 of 11 surviving infants), that the phase 2 autism trial was negative on its primary outcome (one secondary outcome positive; adverse effects mainly diuretic), and that the phase 3 record gives baseline characteristics only.
p4_card.pharmacology: NKCC1 activity: one fitted value and two single-concentration readings in ChEMBL (values in the README). IT8 P3 2026-10-29: GtoPdb (human, one document) gives pIC50 5.60 for NKCC1 and 6.48 for the kidney transporter, so the drug is about 7.6 fold more potent on the renal target; mouse brain to plasma ratio about 0.015 to 0.02 and efflux at the blood-brain barrier (abstract level); at the single intravenous dose reported, far above the diuretic range, modelled free brain concentrations were in the NKCC1-inhibitory range, and diuretic-range doses do not reach neuronal inhibitory concentrations; a close derivative that does not inhibit NKCC1 reproduces some CNS effects (PMID 30248303), so a CNS effect of the drug is not evidence of NKCC1 action. A systemic bumetanide response therefore requires verification of relevant exposure, that is a free brain concentration in the NKCC1 range of about 1.5 to 2.5 micromolar; arithmetic from the mouse figures (brain unbound fraction 6 to 17 percent for three diuretics, brain to plasma ratio about 0.015 to 0.02) puts the corresponding total brain concentration at about 9 to 42 micromolar, an assumption-bound figure and not a prediction (the neonatal maturation of the barrier and efflux in the Wwox-null model is not addressed by these sources; the human plasma concentration is not stated in the US label excerpt read, so it is UNKNOWN here). The premise test is ex vivo with the drug in the bath, where the NKCC1 range of about 1.5 to 2.5 micromolar is the exposure target.
p4_card.predictions: Registered: if GABA is hyperpolarising in the knockout at the age studied, the card closes; if depolarising, bumetanide at a brain-relevant exposure lowers burst frequency, and a negative result at that exposure does not refute the premise.
