mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Downstream of an unresolved lesion: even a correct ISR readout would change a consequence, not restore WWOX function. Deep recovery would need WWOX restored (card C01). Track B (Q230P class): whether the missing mutant protein state engages the ISR is not measured; nothing here is lesion-specific.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
not_known: Whether any WWOX-deficient human neural system has raised eIF2 alpha phosphorylation or ATF4 protein, with or without a proteotoxic load.
Whether the fly Atf4 rise is upstream of Ldh (no Atf4 perturbation in the paper).

Whether the PERK arm or another eIF2 kinase (the paper's Discussion names GCN1/GCN2) is the one engaged; the two interactome entries behind that naming are a low-score unvalidated GCN1 prey (score 0.133, HEK293T) and a three-spectrum WWOX hit in a PERK proximity list (HEK293-T), neither showing binding or activation. In the one fly PARS2 precedent the engaged kinase was GCN2, with phospho-PERK unchanged, so a PERK-arm inhibitor would not be the matched tool there; which kinase, if any, is engaged in WWOX-deficient neural cells is unmeasured.

Whether an eIF2B activator, which acts downstream of eIF2 alpha phosphorylation and restores translation, would reproduce the genetic GCN2 or ATF4 suppression: the fly precedent does not separate the ATF4-dependent limb from the translation-repression limb and tested no compound.
Whether attenuating the ISR would help or harm a WWOX-deficient developing brain.

Whether an ATF4 protein or P-eIF2a rise in a WWOX-deficient neural system survives silencing of network activity (tetrodotoxin or an mGluR5 antagonist): a 5-minute pulse of a group I mGluR agonist raises both, measured 30 minutes later (n 3, P about 0.045), without an Atf4 mRNA change, in normal mouse hippocampal slices (PMID 41706892; that network activity does so is an inference), and WWOX-deficient systems are hyperexcitable (IT8 P5 loop 1).

Whether the ISR in a WWOX-deficient system is compensatory rather than harmful: in the AFG3L2 precedent (PMID 37804316) DELE1 or HRI siRNA slows the growth of patient fibroblasts in low-glucose culture (neither was removed in mice), and a GADD34-targeted compound slightly improves patient-fibroblast growth in low-glucose culture and, given to the dams around birth and then daily to the pups, extends survival of the knockout mice (about 6 days at the median by plot reading, 5 treated knockouts or a multiple; the authors write 'only 10 days'; eIF2alpha phosphorylation and ATF4 not measured in treated mice), a different direction from the PARS2 fly, with different species, endpoint and manipulation; the AFG3L2 kinase evidence is siRNA in fibroblasts, GCN2 and PERK were not tested, and the compound's target is disputed: an in vitro study with purified PPP1R15A fragments found Sephin1 at the tested concentration without effect on complex association or dissociation (biolayer interferometry) and Sephin1 at escalating concentrations (top concentration not stated in the text or legend) without effect on eIF2alpha-P dephosphorylation, and guanabenz inert at the high concentration tested in the enzymatic assay (PMID 28447936, Figures 7 and 8; ADV-276, 2026-11-25); the authors limit the statement of no direct interference with complex assembly or stability to that experimental system. Attenuators and potentiators are therefore two arms of one open question, not one direction.

Whether ISRIB or any eIF2B activator reaches or acts in a Wwox-deficient neural cell: the database holds one cell-reporter row for ISRIB, no eIF2B row and no exposure value; trazodone has no stress-response row [IT59 2026-11-20 third packet change].

Whether any organoid transcript difference or null on this card (deposit GSE156243) is independent of the CRISPR clone and of the batch: the sequenced knockout organoids are four of ONE clone (1B, from edit-spanning reads, ADV-244, SCI, 2026-11-25), the other clone (A2) was not sequenced, the comparator is two organoids of the parental line (the authors removed two of four wild-type libraries, one for failed quality control and one for not clustering), and the organoids appear to come from one batch (the authors' Methods: organoids from the same batch were used for all analyses unless stated otherwise; their reply to reviewers speaks of the batch of the RNA-seq; not stated as a measured fact for these six libraries), so a difference here is not shown to be a property of the knockout rather than of the clone or the batch. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-244]

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

against: Without amyloid the fly Atf4 comparison was not significant (6 vs 6; no interaction test between backgrounds; not a demonstrated absence).
In the human knockout organoid the ATF4/ISR target transcripts are lower than chance (exploratory, no amyloid).
The ALS trial engaged the target and showed no benefit.
Atf4 is not perturbed in the paper: the Atf4-to-Ldh step is the authors' inference.
The paper reports that Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models, a reminder that attenuating a stress arm has a cost.
for: The fly reports a raised Atf4 signal with Wwox reduction plus amyloid (n 6, one antibody).
An eIF2B activator improved memory and tau in a mouse amyloid model.
A paediatric dataset for an ISR-attenuating drug exists in a different, eIF2B-driven disease.

GENETIC precedent in another disease (Xu 2026, PMID 41380592; read in full, manifest PMID41380592.json entries 1, 3, 30, 33, 34, 35; receipt FTR-20261027-41380592-01): in a fly model of the mitochondrial prolyl-tRNA synthetase lesion behind a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in people, pan-neuronal RNAi against GCN2 lowered the bang-sensitive fraction from about 87 to about 30 percent and RNAi against ATF4 from about 93 to about 46 percent (three vials of ten flies each; ATF4 spread about 30 to 62), and both shortened the developmental delay. Partial rescues, partial knockdowns measured in the single-RNAi lines only, seizure-like behaviour and developmental timing not separable, no compound and no ISRIB-class agent tested, no mitochondrial readout after suppression, sex not stated for the behavioural assay. It is a question-generating precedent for the ISR need, not a WWOX experiment and not a pharmacological result.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Amyloid load is the context of the fly effect; WWOX-DEE has no stated amyloid load. Adult neurodegeneration trials do not transfer to a developmental encephalopathy. The fly PARS2 precedent (the genetic precedent in the for-list) shows that an ISR can be harmful when a mitochondrial translation lesion drives it and says nothing about whether WWOX loss drives it: no link between WWOX and mitochondrial translation or OXPHOS protein abundance is established by any source read for this card.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. If the ISR were elevated and harmful, attenuation could protect function; if it is adaptive, attenuation could add harm. Neither is measured for WWOX.
p4_card.identity: ISR attenuators: eIF2B activators (ISRIB and its clinical-stage successors), PERK-arm inhibitors, and repurposed compounds that reverse eIF2 alpha-P-mediated translational repression; guanabenz as the paediatric-experience member. Full per-compound table: lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md section 2.1.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a WWOX-dependent ISR elevation is shown in a human neural system. Today the transfer rests on a fly amyloid model; the one human knockout transcriptome does not show the signature. No Q230P or null-allele datum exists.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: eIF2B (five-subunit complex, EIF2B1-5, HGNC:3257-3261) or the PERK arm (EIF2AK3, HGNC:3255); direction: attenuate the ISR; context: amyloid-stressed fly neurons in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE.
p4_card.next_measurement: Stage 1 (decides everything after it): eIF2 alpha phosphorylation, ATF4 protein and ATF4-target transcripts in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity, with and without a defined proteotoxic challenge. If not elevated, park with the reopening condition below. Stage 2 (only if elevated): an eIF2B activator versus vehicle on that readout and on one functional endpoint. In the fly: an Atf4 loss-of-function arm with the Ldh and lactate readouts. Readout design (added 2026-10-27 from the fly PARS2 reading): read the eIF2 kinases separately (phospho-GCN2 and phospho-PERK, not phospho-eIF2 alpha alone), read OXPHOS subunit protein abundance as a covariate because the one precedent ISR is driven by a mitochondrial translation lesion, and keep a basal-ISR-tone control (in that precedent GCN2 RNAi alone lowered phospho-eIF2 alpha below control). IT8 P5 additions (design only): (a) run every ATF4 protein and P-eIF2a read with and without activity silencing; (b) sample before, at and after the first network hyperexcitability (organoids: weeks 7, 10, 16) to order any rise against the network phenotype; (c) read OMA1 and OPA1 processing as an HRI-arm trigger readout that needs no DELE1 antibody; (d) only if Stage 1 is positive, test a potentiating arm beside the attenuating arm, with a target-engagement control for any GADD34-targeted compound, and read the isogenic corrected line beside the knock-out.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an ISR modulator to WWOX deficiency; coverage is DGIdb, ChEMBL, Open Targets, PubTator 3 gene censuses and eight PubMed searches on 2026-10-26, and DGIdb, ChEMBL and Open Targets are themselves empty for the eIF2B activators. A zero is a statement about those queries.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE (partial benefit through a downstream lever); Track A (variant-independent), Track B conditional and unmeasured.
p4_card.pharmacology: Per compound in compounds_and_sources.md: no eIF2B activity in ChEMBL for ISRIB or fosigotifator; DGIdb and Open Targets empty for the eIF2B complex; PERK inhibitors have enzyme potency in ChEMBL. Added class-level facts, no dose, no score, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE [IT59 2026-11-20 third packet change] (HE ADV-098 batches 7 and 8, public-database rows, hypothesis level): ISRIB is not found by name in the identity tool and is identified by structure; the database holds ONE row for it, an ATF4 reporter in human H4 cells after 24 hours with an IC50 of 2.7 nanomolar (one document): a cell readout of the stress-response output, not a binding and not an eIF2B measurement. No eIF2B activity row, no binding or selectivity row, no value in neurons and none from a second laboratory were found by those routes (not found by these routes is not absence); no measured brain or plasma concentration of ISRIB was found, and the one PubMed hit for brain pharmacokinetics was an unrelated neuropathology paper by its title. No label is expected (a research compound). TRAZODONE: the database holds 284 rows, with 5-HT2A, 5-HT1A, D2 and 5-HT2B among the main groups; no row measures PERK, eIF2 alpha phosphorylation or any integrated stress response assay, so the stress-response link is the literature's and not measured here; two papers disagree by title (a 2017 mouse report that repurposed drugs targeting eIF2 alpha phosphorylation prevent neurodegeneration, and a 2025 paper titled as reporting that trazodone, dibenzoylmethane and tauroursodeoxycholic acid do not prevent motor dysfunction and neurodegeneration (the sheet cuts the title; neither read)). The serotonin 5-HT2A potency differs about twelve-fold by assay type on the sheet's figure (a binding IC50 of 20 nanomolar against 243 nanomolar in a cyclic-AMP assay), so the same receptor does not give one number. Label (openFDA record, newest 2026-07-14): adults with major depressive disorder; safety and effectiveness in the paediatric population not established, with the antidepressant boxed warning on suicidality in children.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked ISR readout that a compound moves: ATF4 protein and eIF2 alpha phosphorylation (and ATF4-target transcripts) in WWOX-deficient human neural cells at matched maturity, with and without a defined proteotoxic challenge; then a functional endpoint (network, synaptic or myelin) after eIF2B activation.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX. In the fly, Atf4 signal rises only with Wwox reduction plus amyloid and Atf4 is never perturbed. In the one human knockout transcriptome the ISR target set is lower than chance (exploratory).
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly amyloid model with partial RNAi; one human knockout transcriptome without amyloid; every compound datum is from another disease, mostly adult.

drug_assertions.endpoint: cellular effect of stiripentol versus enzyme-level LDH inhibition
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: In U87 glioblastoma cells (PMID 42035940) viability falls at 10 to 60 micromolar stiripentol over 48 h and extracellular acidification falls at 25 to 50 micromolar over 24 h; in the two mouse small-cell lung cancer lines of the complex I paper (mSCLC 2405 and 1578; PMID 41570991) viability by annexin V and propidium iodide was not significantly changed at 250 micromolar and was lower at 500 micromolar (Supplementary Fig 1B, n 3). LDH activity in a lysate of treated cells and on recombinant enzyme falls only at hundreds of micromolar (the size of the lysate inhibition is not in the text and no LDH IC50 exists). NADH-driven oxygen consumption of permeabilised mouse mitochondria, with complex I as the entry point (six concentrations, 25 to 150 micromolar), falls in heart to about 48 percent remaining at 25 micromolar and about 5 percent at 100 micromolar (n 4), and in liver to about 67, 38 and 24 percent at 25, 100 and 150 micromolar (n 3; first marked significant at 100 micromolar); plot readings, about 3 points of uncertainty. The same paper also measures NADH-dependent activity two ways in permeabilised mouse heart mitochondria: INT dye reduction (inhibited by stiripentol, not by rotenone) and duroquinone NADH oxidation followed at 340 nanometres (inhibited by both stiripentol and rotenone) (Fig 6B, 6D); a Q2-based NADH-oxidation assay was run on yeast mitochondria, where stiripentol did not inhibit the Nde or Ndi activity (Fig 6E, 6F); no assay compares the two, so potencies are not comparable (INFERENZA: the effective concentrations are ordered complex I below LDH). The text figure of about 70 percent inhibition at 100 micromolar refers to intact uncoupled mouse small-cell lung cancer cells, not mitochondria (Supplementary Fig 2, where the plot reads 51 to 53 percent raw; 100 micromolar is the second of four concentrations). The complex I paper reports no inhibition of malate dehydrogenase. Genetic LDHA/B double knockout raises respiratory capacity whereas stiripentol lowers it, so the drug does not phenocopy LDH ablation on respiration (INFERENZA). Cellular effects of stiripentol are therefore not attributable to LDH alone on the available data (the 2026 glioblastoma paper itself reports 'at least a partial role' of LDH). In a mouse glioblastoma xenograft stiripentol prolonged survival (log-rank P 0.002; median survival 80 days for control and 97 for treated as printed, while the study's source data (published Figure 6F; 16 control and 15 treated animals) give 95 for the treated arm; human stem-like cells in immunodeficient mice. Results and legend state one dose and the Methods another, which the authors' peer-review reply identifies as an earlier experiment replaced by the published one; direction and test unchanged; 2026-11-25, ADV-279, SCI reading). None of the sources states which stereoisomer was used. Tumour models: no seizure, neurodevelopment or WWOX meaning.

evidence_against: Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models (the authors' own citation).
Weak LDH inhibition by stiripentol in the retrieved measurements (a weak measure is not general inefficacy: assay, substrate level and enzyme source differ, and the 2015 report is unread).
Direct inhibition of mitochondrial complex I by stiripentol, so a metabolic effect is not an LDH effect.

An Ldh abundance rise also accompanies a complex I-reduced, ISR-activated fly model that has neither WWOX nor amyloid (DA-PARS2-LDH-001), so a raised Ldh in a Wwox-reduced fly does not by itself identify an LDH-specific lesion (INFERENZA: possible confounding by mitochondrial or ISR state).

Human lactate in WWOX deficiency: blood normal where stated (5 publications, up to 14 subjects, no values printed); spectroscopy mixed (one report with small peaks in early infancy and none later, one report 'extremely low', confounded by a second candidate variant); one raised value in the registry is without a held source passage. [IT 2026-11-25, ADV-255 via SCI]

IT7 P3/P1 (exploratory, independently verified): in an independent WWOX-loss contrast (P47T hippocampus) the LDH isoforms split (LDHA +0.48, LDHB -0.10 against the build direction) and the six-gene module lies inside its null (p 0.060), so the LDHA elevation is not shown to be a reproducible WWOX-loss feature; the signed network and the network labelled WWOX-enriched in IT7 (four duplicated HIF1A edges, already in the external network; the comparison therefore tests nothing about WWOX knowledge in general, and no added value was measurable) showed no added value for ranking compounds on this module and the signature route was not detected, not excluded, and stiripentol was outside that comparison by design. A computational result, not engagement data.

not_known: Whether lactate or LDH activity is altered in WWOX-deficient human neural cells, independent of maturity.
Whether stiripentol engages LDH in brain at tolerated exposures (the 2015 report is the claimed source and was not readable; its exposure and enzyme numbers are unknown here).
What the real potency of stiripentol on LDH is: only single-concentration measurements exist and no fitted value.
Which of stiripentol's effects on tumour-cell metabolism and respiration are LDH-mediated and which act through complex I.

Whether complex I inhibition at the exposures that matter itself recruits the integrated stress response and raises Ldh abundance in neural cells. In a fly model with reduced complex I protein, raised phospho-eIF2 alpha and an Ldh rise (DA-PARS2-LDH-001) that is the observed association and not a test; acute pharmacological inhibition is not the same perturbation, so the link is a question for the complex I arm, not a result.
Whether Ldh lowering is beneficial or harmful without the amyloid context.
Why lactate falls nominally with Wwox reduction without amyloid.

Whether any organoid transcript difference or null on this card (deposit GSE156243) is independent of the CRISPR clone and of the batch: the sequenced knockout organoids are four of ONE clone (1B, from edit-spanning reads, ADV-244, SCI, 2026-11-25), the other clone (A2) was not sequenced, the comparator is two organoids of the parental line (the authors removed two of four wild-type libraries, one for failed quality control and one for not clustering), and the organoids appear to come from one batch (the authors' Methods: organoids from the same batch were used for all analyses unless stated otherwise; their reply to reviewers speaks of the batch of the RNA-seq; not stated as a measured fact for these six libraries), so a difference here is not shown to be a property of the knockout rather than of the clone or the batch. against: The Ldh rescue lacks an Ldh-alone arm, a Wwox-mRNA check and a lactate readout, and the authors cite Ldh knockdown as detrimental in other fly amyloid models.
Without amyloid lactate falls nominally and Ldh does not change.

Stiripentol inhibits LDH only weakly in the single-concentration measurements held (none gives a fitted potency, and the one at the highest concentration is the lowest), and it has other targets, including direct inhibition of mitochondrial complex I, that act at lower concentrations; any benefit would not be attributable to LDH.
LDHA in the organoid is as consistent with immaturity as with WWOX loss.
Human lactate in WWOX deficiency is reported normal or extremely low.

IT7 P3/P1 (exploratory, independently verified): in an independent WWOX-loss contrast (P47T hippocampus) the LDH isoforms split (LDHA +0.48, LDHB -0.10 against the build direction) and the six-gene module lies inside its null (p 0.060), so the LDHA elevation is not shown to be a reproducible WWOX-loss feature; the signed network and the network labelled WWOX-enriched in IT7 (four duplicated HIF1A edges, already in the external network; the comparison therefore tests nothing about WWOX knowledge in general, and no added value was measurable) showed no added value for ranking compounds on this module and the signature route was not detected, not excluded, and stiripentol was outside that comparison by design. A computational result, not engagement data.

IT8 P3 (2026-10-29), corrected 2026-11-26: for stiripentol as a way to test the LDH node, the enzyme-level data are weak and no potency has been fitted - 7 percent inhibition of both human LDH5 and LDH1 at 2 millimolar (ChEMBL document CHEMBL4311969; the same document lists two 0.5 millimolar LDH rows with no value), 9.9 percent for the racemate at 0.5 millimolar in an independent report (Rico-Molina 2024) whose two enantiomers give 34 and 38 percent at the same concentration (the racemate lies below both, so the three figures are not mutually consistent; all three IC50 are printed as above 500 micromolar), about 40 percent at 0.5 millimolar attributed to Sada 2015 (second-hand), and an LDH assay on lysate of U87 glioblastoma cells that had been exposed to stiripentol, with LDH added per well (so not a direct enzyme-inhibition test), whose inhibition the authors call moderate, significant only at 250 and 500 micromolar, with no percentage given in the text (PMID 42035940); no fitted LDH potency among the 88 database rows read for it; a label that does not name LDH; the database cell-level signal (mouse hepatocyte oxalate output at 10 micromolar: four rows, two cell models at 24 and 48 hours, relative output 0.27 to 0.70, in an assay labelled GO/LDHA, so shared with glycolate oxidase) is not LDH engagement; the third report (Sada 2015) remains abstract-only and secondary.
for: Ldh RNAi improved climbing in the amyloid-plus-Wwox-reduction fly genotype (once).
Ldh transcript and lactate rise together in that genotype.

Stiripentol is an approved paediatric epilepsy drug with an LDH link published in epilepsy models (2015 report; abstract-level here) and an LDH-directed analogue series exists; nedosiran shows LDHA lowering is tolerated in humans in the liver.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: The fly effect needs amyloid; stiripentol's approved use depends on co-administration with another antiseizure drug and does not establish brain LDH engagement.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. A partial locomotor benefit was seen once in the fly with Ldh RNAi; no human or WWOX datum.
p4_card.identity: LDH-directed levers: stiripentol (approved for a paediatric developmental epilepsy; weak LDH inhibition in vitro), GSK2837808A and other research LDHA inhibitors, and the LDHA-directed oligonucleotide nedosiran (approved for primary hyperoxaluria, liver-directed). Per-compound table: compounds_and_sources.md section 2.2.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF lactate or LDH activity is shown to be a driver in a WWOX-deficient human neural system. The one fly precedent is amyloid-conditional; human lactate readouts in WWOX deficiency are normal or low in the cited sources (DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009).
p4_card.mechanism: Target: LDHA (HGNC:6535, P00338) and LDHB (HGNC:6541, P07195); direction: lower LDH activity or lactate production; context: amyloid-stressed fly head in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE. For stiripentol the LDH link is not the established basis of its antiseizure use.
p4_card.next_measurement: IT7 P6 2026-10-29: read LDHA and LDHB activity separately (LDHB was the discordant gene in the P47T transfer test); no computational ranking selects the compound arm. In the fly: lactate (enantiomer- or isotope-resolved) in the Ldh-RNAi double genotype, an Ldh-alone arm, and Wwox mRNA in the double line. In human neural cells: LDH activity and the lactate-to-pyruvate relationship in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic cells at matched maturity. Only then a compound arm. IT8 P3 2026-10-29, restated IT9 P4a 2026-10-30, corrected 2026-11-26: stiripentol is not sufficiently supported as an LDH-engagement probe, because the enzyme-level data are weak and no potency has been fitted (7 percent inhibition at 2 millimolar; 9.9 percent for the racemate at 0.5 millimolar; the fuller list is in the evidence against), the US label names no LDH mechanism, and the cell-level readings found (four rows of a 2022 glycolate-oxidase and LDHA double-inhibitor series: relative oxalate output 0.27 to 0.70 at 10 micromolar in mouse hepatocytes; in the papers read, lactate production about halved at 500 micromolar and extracellular acidification and oxygen consumption lower at 25 and 50 micromolar in glioblastoma cells, and lower oxalate output in HepG2 cells at 5 to 100 micrograms per millilitre) do not separate LDH from other actions (complex I inhibition for the glioblastoma readings, Bouchez 2026; glycolate oxidase for the hepatocyte series), so they do not establish LDH engagement; the HepG2 report also gives lower urine oxalate in rats and patients, which is not direct LDH engagement either; all 88 curated rows for the racemate were read, 8 concern LDH (4 enzyme-level, 4 cell-level) and none is a fitted LDH potency; the 42 to 500 micromolar range quoted for it is a secondary figure. The arm is a nanomolar human-LDHA inhibitor taken from the curated database target entries: 205 qualify, 116 have no LDHB datum at all (unknown, not non-selective) and, of the 89 with a same-document, same-activity-type LDHA and LDHB pair, 74 have a pair under 10 fold and only 2 are 30 fold or more on every pair, so selectivity over LDHB must be established per compound (list by id in qualification_it9_p4a_20261030/ldha_nanomolar_selectivity.tsv); stiripentol is kept as a complex I and GABA-A comparator so that its other pharmacology is separable from LDH. Readout design (added 2026-10-27 from the fly PARS2 reading): in every arm that perturbs complex I, read the integrated stress response (phospho-eIF2 alpha, ATF4 protein) and Ldh abundance next to Ldh ACTIVITY and lactate, because abundance, activity, metabolite level and flux are separate quantities and a complex I perturbation may raise Ldh abundance through the stress response. The designed comparison (question, model, controls, endpoint, result that would change interpretation) is in sada_ldh_precedent_p2a_20261026.md section 6; it is a proposal, nothing is authorised to run.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an LDH inhibitor to WWOX deficiency; coverage is the six sources of compounds_and_sources.md and ten PubMed abstracts on 2026-10-26. Update 2026-10-26 (scientist-b, P2a): the 2015 report usually cited for stiripentol and LDH in epilepsy (PMID 25792327) is now identified, is paywalled with no lawful full text found, and is known here only through its abstract and three open-access secondary descriptions; it is a stiripentol-LDH precedent in epilepsy models, not a WWOX datum.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Stiripentol label: indicated for Dravet syndrome seizures in patients taking clobazam, from six months of age (openFDA label 2026-04-27); the same label means any use here would sit on top of clobazam co-therapy, an interaction this card does not assess. No paediatric suitability for WWOX-DEE is presumed.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A, Track B untested.
p4_card.pharmacology: Stiripentol: marketed formulation with a paediatric label for Dravet syndrome with clobazam; weak LDH inhibition in single-concentration enzyme measurements (no fitted potency; sizes differ between racemate, enantiomers and a database document), effective concentrations for LDH above total plasma levels and far above estimated free tissue levels in a review, other targets at lower concentrations; brain LDH engagement in vivo is asserted by secondary sources citing the 2015 report but not verified here. IT8 P3 2026-10-29 (ChEMBL molecule-first on the racemate: 28 rows under the type filter IC50, Ki, Kd, EC50, Kb, Potency and Inhibition, 88 unfiltered, none a fitted LDH potency; one comparator document with LDH5 and LDH1 inhibition of 7 percent at 2 millimolar and no value at 0.5 millimolar; four cell-level rows of another document, mouse hepatocyte oxalate output 0.27 to 0.70 at 10 micromolar, a pathway shared with glycolate oxidase, weighed and not decisive; the US label of 2026-04-27 states that the human mechanism is unknown and names GABA-A and cytochrome P450 inhibition as possible mechanisms, gives protein binding of 99 percent and no peak concentration). GSK2837808A: potent on LDHA in vitro, no in vivo or CNS datum retrieved. Nedosiran: liver-directed.

Status, F/C/P position and the premise are unchanged.
